definition_zh: 记号；痕迹；标记；符号；分数；留下痕迹；注意
definition_en: a small visible trace or spot; a written sign or symbol; a grade given for schoolwork; to leave a visible trace; to notice or pay attention to
core_image: 一支红笔在纸页角落画下一个小小的圈
scene: 海图摊在桌上，灯下的纸页已经发黄，边角还有折过的痕迹。A red mark on the chart showed where the ship had struck the reef.
sceneCN: 这里指留在纸面上的可见痕迹（第 1 个义项：记号、痕迹）；句意为海图上的一处红色记号标出了船撞上礁石的位置。

senses.title: A visible spot or line left on a surface
senses.definition: a small area of damage, colour or dirt that shows something has touched or pressed a surface
senses.definitionCN: 表面上一小块颜色、污迹或破损，显示有东西接触或压过
senses.example: A red mark on the chart showed where the ship had struck the reef.
senses.exampleCN: 海图上的一处红色记号标出了船撞上礁石的位置。
senses.why: Old English mearc first named a boundary sign, a visible thing set down to show where something is or has happened, and that visible trace is the core of the word.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 mearc 最初指边界的标志，是一件看得见的东西，用来说明某物在哪里或发生过什么；这种可见的痕迹就是这个词的核心。

senses.title: A written sign or symbol
senses.definition: a sign, symbol or written figure used to represent something or to give information
senses.definitionCN: 用来代表某物或提供信息的符号、记号或书写图样
senses.example: Put a mark beside the name of the candidate you prefer.
senses.exampleCN: 在你更中意的候选人名字旁边做一个标记。
senses.why: Once a visible sign can stand for something other than itself, the boundary trace becomes a symbol, and writing turns that symbol into a small reusable unit of meaning.
senses.whyCN: 当一件可见的标记能够代表它自身以外的东西，边界痕迹就变成符号，而文字又把这个符号变成可反复使用的小单位。

senses.title: A score or grade given for work
senses.definition: a number or letter showing how well a piece of schoolwork or a performance has been judged
senses.definitionCN: 表示某份作业或某次表现被评为多好的数字或字母
senses.example: She was pleased with the mark she received on the essay.
senses.exampleCN: 她对自己的作文分数很满意。
senses.why: A teacher's mark was once a physical sign placed next to an answer; because that sign recorded quality, the sign itself came to mean the judgement written into it.
senses.whyCN: 教师的 mark 原是画在答案旁边的一个实记号；正因为这个记号记录了优劣，记号本身便转而表示写在里面的评判。

senses.title: To leave a visible trace on something
senses.definition: to make a visible spot, line or sign on a surface, often to identify or record something
senses.definitionCN: 在表面上留下可见的点、线或符号，常用来识别或记录
senses.example: She marked the page with a folded corner before returning the book.
senses.exampleCN: 她折了个角给那一页做记号，然后才把书还回去。
senses.why: The verb is the noun put into action: to mark is to produce the very trace that the noun names, and the purpose is usually to make something findable later.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是名词化为动作：mark 某物，就是造出名词所指的那种痕迹，目的通常是让某样东西日后能被找到。

senses.title: To notice or pay attention to
senses.definition: to notice something and give it attention, especially because it deserves to be remembered
senses.definitionCN: 注意到某事并加以关注，尤因它值得被记住
senses.example: Mark my words: the second attempt will be harder than the first.
senses.exampleCN: 记住我的话：第二次尝试会比第一次更难。
senses.why: A mark draws the eye to one spot, so to mark something in speech is to single it out mentally and ask the listener to keep it in view.
senses.whyCN: 记号把目光引向某一处，所以在言语中说 mark 某事，就是在心里把它单独标出，并要求听者一直记着。

intro.en: Mark began as a Germanic word for a boundary sign, and from that visible sign it grew into a trace, a symbol, a grade and an act of attention.
intro.cn: mark 起初是日耳曼语中表示边界标志的词，从那个可见的标志出发，长出痕迹、符号、分数与注意等义。

items.en: The boundary sense is usually traced to a reconstructed root *merg-, meaning a border or edge, though the reconstruction is not certain.
items.cn: 边界义一般认为可追溯到重构词根 *merg-，意为边界、边缘，但这一重构并不完全确定。

items.en: The reconstructed noun *markō meant a boundary and a sign set on it, and it is the base of the English word.
items.cn: 重构名词 *markō 意为边界以及立在边界上的标志，是英语这个词的词基。

items.en: Old English mearc covered a boundary, a landmark and a sign, so the word already joined the idea of an edge to the idea of something visible.
items.cn: 古英语 mearc 同时表示边界、地标和标志，这个词已经把「边缘」与「看得见的东西」连在一起。

items.en: Middle English mark widened to any trace, target or written symbol, and school use added the sense of a judgement written beside an answer.
items.cn: 中古英语 mark 扩展到任何痕迹、目标或书写符号，学校里的用法又增加了「写在答案旁边的评判」这一义。

items.en: Modern English adds the verb of noticing and the compounds marker, bookmark and trademark, while the border sense survives mainly in place names.
items.cn: 现代英语增加了表示「注意」的动词，以及 marker、bookmark、trademark 等复合词，边界义则主要留存在地名里。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on mark and its old boundary root; the near-meaning group gathers words for signs, stains and grades.
note.cn: 形近组收由 mark 及其古老边界词根构成的形式；近义组收表示符号、污迹与分数的词。

entries.definition: Clearly noticeable, or having a mark on it.

entries.definition: An object or link used to keep a place in a book or on a page.
entries.definitionCN: 用来记住书页或网页位置的东西。

entries.definition: A comment; to say something about what one has noticed.
entries.definitionCN: 评论；就注意到的事说些什么。

entries.definition: A symbol, notice or gesture that conveys information.
entries.definitionCN: 传递信息的符号、告示或手势。

entries.definition: A mark or object that represents something else.
entries.definitionCN: 代表另一事物的记号或物件。

entries.definition: A dirty mark left on a surface.

normalIntro.en: The word starts as a boundary sign cut into the ground, becomes any visible trace, and then any symbol, judgement or act of attention.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从刻在地面上的边界标志开始，先变成任何可见的痕迹，再变成符号、评判或注意的动作。

normal.en: Old English mearc meant a boundary and a sign, so the word began with something placed on the ground to show where one thing ends and another begins.
normal.cn: 古英语 mearc 意为边界与标志，所以这个词起初指放在地面上的东西，用来说明一物到何处为止、另一物从何处开始。

normal.en: The same old sense survives in the Welsh marches, a border region, and in the Latin relative margo, a margin or edge.
normal.cn: 同样的旧义留存在威尔士边境这一地名里，也留存在拉丁语近亲 margo（页边、边缘）中。

normal.en: A school mark began as a sign written beside an answer, and the sign came to stand for the judgement it recorded.
normal.cn: 学校的 mark 原是写在答案旁的记号，后来这个记号转而代表它所记录的评判。

normal.en: The verb mark is the noun turned into an action: the trace and the act of making it share one form.
normal.cn: 动词 mark 是名词化为动作：痕迹与留下痕迹的行为共用一种形式。

normal.en: Mark my words uses the physical sign as a mental one: the words are singled out so the listener will not forget them.
normal.cn: Mark my words 把实体的记号用作心里的记号：把话单独标出，让听者不会忘记。

abstract.en: A single red circle can point to a reef, a name or a mistake, because a mark is attention made visible.
abstract.cn: 一个小小的红圈可以指向礁石、名字或错误，因为记号就是被看见的注意。

abstract.en: A boundary and a symbol are the same gesture: something small is placed to say this is where meaning begins.
abstract.cn: 边界与符号是同一个动作：放下某件小小的东西，说「意义从这里开始」。

abstract.en: To mark a word in a book is to ask the page to remember for you.
abstract.cn: 在书里给一个词做记号，就是请纸页替你记住。

examples.en: A red mark on the chart showed where the ship had struck the reef.
examples.cn: 海图上的一处红色记号标出了船撞上礁石的位置。

examples.cn: 在你更中意的候选人名字旁边做一个标记。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a visible trace placed on a surface; the written symbol, the grade, the act of marking and the mental act of noticing all grow from that one visible sign.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是留在表面上的可见痕迹；书写符号、分数、做记号的动作以及心里的留意，都从这同一个可见标志长出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a small red circle drawn in the corner of a page.

definition_zh: 市场；集市；某种商品的交易领域；销路、需求；股市；行销、推销
definition_en: a place or system in which goods and services are bought and sold, or the willingness of buyers to purchase them
core_image: 清晨的集市街：木棚下摆着成筐的果子，一杆秤搁在摊边，买主与卖主在摊前讨价
scene: 天刚亮，街边木棚下摆满果筐，买卖双方在摊前讨价。Growers bring their produce to a market where buyers bargain over each crate.
sceneCN: 前半情境：天刚亮，街边木棚下摆满果筐，买卖双方在摊前讨价；句中的 market 指「买卖双方定期相聚的集市场地」（第 1 个义项：作为交易场所的集市）。图中可辨识物件：木棚、果筐、杆秤、写价的木牌；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: A place where buyers and sellers meet
senses.titleCN: 买卖双方相聚的集市场地
senses.definition: an open place, often with stalls, where people regularly come together to buy and sell goods
senses.definitionCN: 常设有摊位的露天场所，人们定期在此相聚买卖货物
senses.example: Farmers set up stalls at the weekly market.
senses.exampleCN: 农民每周在集市上摆摊。
senses.why: the Latin noun mercatus named the place and the trading done there, so the word began as a location for exchange.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁名词 mercatus 既指场所也指在那里进行的交易，因此这个词最初就是交换的地点。

senses.title: Trade in one particular commodity
senses.titleCN: 某一种商品的交易领域
senses.definition: the whole body of buying and selling in one commodity or one sector, wherever it happens
senses.definitionCN: 某一种商品或某一部门中全部买卖活动的总和，不论发生在何处
senses.example: The world market for copper tightened last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年世界铜的交易领域收紧了。
senses.why: the place sense was transferred from a square to a field of trade, so that copper can have a market with no square at all.
senses.whyCN: 场所义从一方广场转移到一片交易领域，于是铜可以有市场，而完全不需要广场。

senses.title: Demand for a product
senses.definition: the number of buyers willing to purchase something, or the absence of such buyers
senses.definitionCN: 愿意购买某物的买者数量，或这类买者的缺乏
senses.example: There is little market for hand-written ledgers now.
senses.exampleCN: 如今手写账簿已没什么销路。
senses.why: without buyers a place of exchange is empty, so the word came to mean the willingness to buy rather than the ground it stands on.
senses.whyCN: 没有买主，交换的场所就是空的，于是这个词转而指购买的意愿，而不是它所在的那块地。

senses.title: The market for shares and securities
senses.definition: the organized exchange on which shares, bonds and currencies are traded, or trading there as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 买卖股票、债券与货币的有组织的交易所，或该处的交易整体
senses.example: Share prices fell across the market before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 午前整个股市的股价都下跌了。
senses.why: a stock exchange is a marketplace in the original sense, only with paper claims instead of crates, so the old word was kept.
senses.whyCN: 证券交易所就是原义上的集市，只是货物换成了纸面权益，旧词因此被沿用。

senses.title: Offered for sale
senses.titleCN: 在售；待售（置于售卖状态）
senses.definition: the state of being available to buy, as in a house that has come onto the market
senses.definitionCN: 处于可供购买的状态，如已挂牌出售的房子
senses.example: The building came onto the market in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这栋楼在春天挂牌出售。
senses.why: being placed before buyers is the modern equivalent of being carried to the stalls, and the phrase on the market keeps that image.
senses.whyCN: 被摆到买主面前，相当于旧时把货物挑到摊位上，这一短语保留了那个画面。

senses.title: To sell and promote a product
senses.definition: to promote and sell a product by choosing its buyers, its price and the way it is presented
senses.definitionCN: 通过选择买主、定价与呈现方式来推销并卖出产品
senses.example: The firm markets its software to schools.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司把软件行销给学校。
senses.why: if a market is where goods find buyers, then to market is to do the work of bringing goods and buyers together.
senses.whyCN: 如果市场是货物找到买主的地方，那么行销就是把货物与买主带到一起的工作。

senses.title: The mechanism that sets prices
senses.definition: the system in which prices and quantities are settled by the competing decisions of many buyers and sellers
senses.definitionCN: 价格与数量由众多买卖双方的竞争性决定来敲定的系统
senses.example: The market, not the ministry, decides which suppliers survive.
senses.exampleCN: 决定哪些供应商存活的是市场，而不是部委。
senses.why: abstracting the place away leaves only its function: bringing competing offers together until a price emerges.
senses.whyCN: 把场所抽掉，只剩它的功能：把互相竞争的报价汇集起来，直到价格出现。

senses.title: The body of intended buyers
senses.definition: the group of people or institutions a seller intends to reach, considered as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 卖方打算触及的那一群人或机构，被作为一个整体来看
senses.example: The brand's market is young urban readers.
senses.exampleCN: 这个品牌的目标买方群体是年轻的城市读者。
senses.why: a seller who studies the crowd at the stalls ends by treating that crowd as an object to be served, which is the marketing sense.
senses.whyCN: 研究摊位前人群的卖方，最终把那群人当作服务对象，这就是营销义。

intro.en: Market is Latin in origin, not a native English word: it goes back to Latin mercatus 'market, trading', a noun from the verb mercari 'to trade', which in turn rests on merx (genitive mercis) 'goods'. It reached Old English through Old Northern French and Germanic channels. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: market 是拉丁来源，而非英语本族词：它上溯至拉丁名词 mercatus「市场、集市、交易」，该名词出自动词 mercari「做买卖」，而动词又基于 merx（属格 mercis）「货物」。它经古北法语与日耳曼中介进入古英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Merx, genitive mercis, meant 'goods, merchandise'. Its own deeper origin is uncertain, and no pre-Latin source can be demonstrated.
items.cn: merx（属格 mercis）意为「货物、商品」。它自身更深的来源不确定，无法证明任何拉丁语之前的源头。

items.en: From the noun came the deponent verb mercari 'to buy and sell, to trade', which names the activity rather than the goods.
items.cn: 由这个名词产生异态动词 mercari「买卖、做交易」，命名的是活动而非货物。

items.en: The noun mercatus 'market, marketplace, trading' was formed on the same stem, so place and activity were one word from the start.
items.cn: 名词 mercatus「市场、集市、交易」由同一词干构成，因此场所与活动从一开始就是一个词。

items.en: The form market is generally thought to have come to England through Old Northern French, with Germanic channels also involved in its spread.
items.cn: 一般认为 market 这一形式经古北法语传入英格兰，其传播也涉及日耳曼中介。

items.en: Old English already had market as a loanword, which is why the word counts as Latin in origin rather than as an inherited native term.
items.cn: 古英语已经以借词形式拥有 market，因此这个词算作拉丁来源，而非承继的本族词。

items.en: From the physical fair the word widened to trade in one commodity, to demand, to the share market and finally to the verb for promoting goods.
items.cn: 从有形的集市出发，这个词扩展到单一商品的交易、需求、股票市场，最后扩展到推销货物的动词义。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin root, so their kinship is real and can be traced; group two holds near neighbours that all name places or gatherings for trade.
note.cn: 第一组的词同出拉丁词根，亲缘关系真实可溯；第二组是同样指交易场所或聚会的近邻词。

entries.definition: Through Old French from Latin mercari: a person who trades, so it shares the root for 'goods' with market and adds an agent suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 经古法语来自拉丁 mercari：做买卖的人，与本词同出「货物」这一词根，只多了一个施事后缀。

entries.definition: From merx 'goods' through Old French: the goods themselves, which is the root meaning in concrete form.
entries.definitionCN: 经古法语来自 merx「货物」：货物本身，正是该词根的具体形态。

entries.definition: From Italian mercante, from Latin mercari: relating to trade, a later borrowing of the same root rather than a new coinage.
entries.definitionCN: 经意大利语来自拉丁 mercari：关于贸易的，是同一词根的后期借入，而非新造词。

entries.definition: Com- 'together' plus merx: trade viewed as an organized exchange between parties, another descendant of the same root.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中表示「共同」的前缀加 merx：把贸易看作各方之间有组织的交换，是同一词根的另一支后裔。

entries.definition: Market plus place: the square or platform where trading happens, narrower than market because it has no demand or share-price senses.
entries.definitionCN: 由 market 与表示「地方」的成分复合而成：发生交易的广场或平台，比本词窄，因为不含需求与股价等义。

entries.definition: From Latin feria 'holiday': a periodic, often seasonal gathering for trade, with none of the abstract economic senses of market.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 feria「节日」：定期、常为季节性的交易聚会，不含本词那些抽象经济义。

entries.definition: From Persian through Turkish: a covered street of shops, a place word only and never a verb.
entries.definitionCN: 经土耳其语来自波斯语：有顶棚的店铺街，只作场所词，从不用作动词。

entries.definition: A shortened form of market kept for names and poetry; it retains only the place sense.
entries.definitionCN: market 的缩略形式，多用于名称与诗歌，只保留场所义。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives rather than invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The chain runs goods, then trade, then place: merx, mercari, mercatus.
normal.cn: 链条是货物、交易、场所：merx、mercari、mercatus。

normal.en: The family runs market, marketing, marketplace, marketer, marketable, marketization.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 market、marketing、marketplace、marketer、marketable、marketization。

normal.en: Fixed phrases separate the senses: on the market, market share, market forces, stock market.
normal.cn: 固定搭配分开各个义项：在售、市场份额、市场力量、股票市场。

normal.en: The same root shows in merchant, merchandise, mercantile and commerce.
normal.cn: 同一词根出现在 merchant、merchandise、mercantile 与 commerce 中。

normal.en: The verb takes an object: to market a product, and the -ing form is the noun marketing.
normal.cn: 动词要带宾语：把产品行销出去，其动名词形式就是名词「营销」。

abstract.en: Picture a square that is crowded at dawn and swept clean by noon.
abstract.cn: 想象一方广场，黎明时挤满人，到正午已被扫空。

abstract.en: Picture two columns on a page: what buyers want, and what they will pay.
abstract.cn: 想象纸页上两栏：买主想要什么，愿意付多少。

abstract.en: Picture a board of share prices where one company's fate becomes a single flashing number.
abstract.cn: 想象一块股价牌，一家公司的命运变成一个闪动的数字。

examples.en: The fishing market opens before sunrise and is empty by noon.
examples.cn: 鱼市在日出前开张，到正午便空了。

examples.en: A product with no market cannot survive, however carefully it is made.
examples.cn: 无论做得多用心，没有销路的产品都活不下去。

examples.en: The cooperative markets its coffee directly to roasters abroad.
examples.cn: 这家合作社把咖啡直接行销给国外的烘焙商。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马克」的谐音——集市上每件货物都用马克笔标上价钱 → 市场

root: 拉丁 merx（属格 mercis）「货物」→ 动词 mercari「做买卖」→ 名词 mercatus「市场、集市、交易」→ 经古北法语与日耳曼中介借入古英语 market；merx 更深来源不确定，故为拉丁来源而非英语本族词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one building: goods (merx) are traded (mercari) in a place (mercatus). From the dawn square the line moves to trade in a single commodity, to the demand that fills or empties the square, to the share market that inherited the name, to the state of being offered for sale, to the verb that brings goods and buyers together, to the price-setting mechanism abstracted from the square, and finally to the crowd of buyers a seller sets out to serve.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一座建筑展开：货物在某个场所里被交易。从黎明时的广场出发，这条线依次走向单一商品的交易、决定广场空与满的需求、继承了这个名称的股票市场、被摆出来售卖的状态、把货物与买主带到一起的动词、从广场抽象出来的定价机制，最后走向卖方打算服务的那群买主。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dawn market square where crates change hands and the crowd thins by noon.
core.cn: 核心意象：黎明的集市广场，成筐货物易手，到正午人群渐散。

branches.en: PLACE AND COMMODITY: a square for exchange becomes a field of trade in one good.
branches.cn: 场所与商品：用于交换的广场变成某一种商品的交易领域。

branches.en: DEMAND AND SHARES: buyers make the square alive, and paper claims inherit its name.
branches.cn: 需求与证券：买主让广场有生气，纸面权益则继承了它的名称。

branches.en: OFFER AND PROMOTE: goods are placed before buyers, and someone must bring them there.
branches.cn: 摆出与推销：货物被摆到买主面前，而总得有人把它们带到那里。

branches.en: ALLOCATION: strip away the square and what remains is a mechanism that settles prices.
branches.cn: 配置：把广场抽走，剩下的就是一个敲定价格的机制。

branches.en: BUYER GROUP: the crowd at the stalls becomes the audience a seller intends to reach.
branches.cn: 买方群体：摊位前的人群变成卖方打算触及的对象。

intro.en: The word is a Latin root for 'goods' dressed in noun and verb endings, with English suffixes building the modern family on top.
intro.cn: 这个词是「货物」这一拉丁词根加上名词与动词词尾，再由英语后缀在其上搭起现代词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin merx and its verb mercari supply the stem; mercatus, the noun of place and activity, is the direct ancestor of the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 merx 及其动词 mercari 提供词干；指场所与活动的名词 mercatus 则是英语这个词的直接祖先。

items.example: The root supplies the idea of goods in every member of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根为词族中每个成员提供「货物」这一观念。

items.example: Merx names what is carried to the stalls.
items.exampleCN: merx 指被挑到摊位上的东西。

items.structure: mercari, mercatus sum (Latin deponent verb, first conjugation)
items.meaning: to trade, to buy and sell
items.example: The verb turns goods into an activity.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把货物变成一种活动。

items.example: The noun carries both the place and the dealing.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词同时承载场所与交易。

items.meaning: a place or system of exchange
items.example: Old English already used the borrowed noun.
items.exampleCN: 古英语已经使用这个借入的名词。

items.example: The compound keeps only the place sense.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词只保留场所义。

items.example: Marketing grew out of the verb to market.
items.exampleCN: 营销由动词「行销」发展而来。

items.meaning: the process or activity of doing
items.example: The suffix turns the verb into a trade activity.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把动词变成一种行业活动。

items.example: Only marketable varieties reached the stalls.
items.exampleCN: 只有可销售的品种被送上摊位。

items.example: The suffix marks what can be sold.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀标出能够被卖出之物。

latinEntries.structure: mercari, mercatus sum (deponent verb, first conjugation)
latinEntries.meaning: to trade, to buy and sell

definition_zh: 两个人依法律或习俗结成的夫妻关系，也指确立这种关系的婚礼
definition_en: the legally or socially recognized union of two people as spouses, and the ceremony that establishes it
core_image: 一张铺着红纸的桌上并排放着两只旧戒指、一份证书和一把新房钥匙
scene: 老屋的堂屋里点着两支红烛，墙上贴着一张写满吉利话的纸。Her grandparents' marriage began with a ceremony that lasted three days.
sceneCN: 这里 marriage 指「两人依俗结成的夫妻结合」（第 1 个义项：由仪式与公认确立的配偶关系）；句意为她祖父母的婚姻始于一场持续三天的婚礼。可辨识物件：红烛、喜字、戒指、证书、钥匙；对应第 1 个义项。

senses.title: The recognized union of spouses
senses.titleCN: 被法律或社会承认的夫妻结合
senses.definition: the state in which two people are legally or socially recognized as spouses
senses.definitionCN: 两个人被法律或社会承认为配偶的状态
senses.example: Their marriage was registered at the county office in spring.
senses.exampleCN: 他们的婚姻是春天在县里登记的。
senses.why: from Latin maritus 'husband', the noun names the wedded state itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词来自拉丁 maritus「丈夫」，直接指已婚状态本身。

senses.title: The wedding ceremony itself
senses.definition: the event in which vows are exchanged and the union is publicly made
senses.definitionCN: 交换誓言并公开确立结合的那场活动
senses.example: The whole village came to the marriage and stayed for the feast.
senses.exampleCN: 全村人都来参加婚礼，并留下来吃喜宴。
senses.why: the event and the state share one word because the rite is what creates the relation.
senses.whyCN: 仪式与状态共用一个词，因为正是仪式造成了这层关系。

senses.title: The ongoing state of being wed
senses.definition: the daily condition of living as a married couple over many years
senses.definitionCN: 多年来作为夫妻共同生活的日常状态
senses.example: Thirty years of marriage had taught them how to argue without wounding.
senses.exampleCN: 三十年的婚姻教会他们如何争吵却不伤人。
senses.why: the noun covers duration, not only the moment of union.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词涵盖持续时间，而不只是结合的那一刻。

senses.title: A type of marriage system
senses.definition: a socially defined form such as monogamy or polygyny, studied as a rule of the group
senses.definitionCN: 如一夫一妻或一夫多妻这类被社会定义的制度，作为群体规则来研究
senses.example: The community practiced marriage between cross-cousins.
senses.exampleCN: 这个社群实行交叉表亲之间的婚姻。
senses.why: societies classify forms of union, and the same noun labels the type.
senses.whyCN: 社会会给结合形式分类，同一个名词也就用来指类型。

senses.title: A close alliance between things
senses.titleCN: 事物之间的紧密结合（比喻义）
senses.definition: a metaphor for two different elements joined so closely that neither keeps its old shape
senses.definitionCN: 比喻两种不同成分紧密结合，彼此都不再保持原样
senses.example: The album is a marriage of folk melody and electronic rhythm.
senses.exampleCN: 这张专辑是民歌曲调与电子节奏的结合。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the core idea of two parties becoming one.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了「两方成为一体」的核心意思。

senses.title: A card game of matching pairs
senses.definition: a card game in which players collect matching pairs, named after the paired union
senses.definitionCN: 玩家收集同名对子的一种纸牌游戏，因配对而成名
senses.example: The old men played marriage beside the stove all evening.
senses.exampleCN: 老人们整晚在炉边玩配对纸牌。
senses.why: the game is named for the matched pair, echoing the union sense.
senses.whyCN: 这种游戏因成对的牌而得名，与「结合」义呼应。

senses.title: A religious sacrament
senses.definition: the union regarded as a sacred vow rather than only a civil contract
senses.definitionCN: 被视为神圣誓约、而非仅是民事契约的结合
senses.example: The church treats marriage as a vow made before God.
senses.exampleCN: 教会把婚姻视为在神面前立下的誓约。
senses.why: religions read the union as sacred, adding a layer the law does not supply.
senses.whyCN: 宗教把这种结合读作神圣的，添加了法律不提供的一层。

senses.title: A political alliance between families
senses.definition: a union arranged to bind two families, courts or states rather than two individuals
senses.definitionCN: 为联结两个家族、宫廷或国家而非两个个人而安排的婚姻
senses.example: The treaty was sealed by a marriage between the two courts.
senses.exampleCN: 条约由两个宫廷之间的联姻加以巩固。
senses.why: kinship was once a diplomatic instrument, and the noun named that instrument.
senses.whyCN: 亲属关系曾是外交工具，这个词就指那件工具。

senses.title: The legal registration of the union
senses.titleCN: 婚姻的法律登记与效力
senses.definition: the recorded act that gives the union standing in courts and in inheritance law
senses.definitionCN: 使这种结合在法院与继承法中生效的登记行为
senses.example: Without registration, the marriage had no standing in court.
senses.exampleCN: 没有登记，这段婚姻在法庭上不具效力。
senses.why: modern states turn the relation into a recorded fact with legal consequences.
senses.whyCN: 现代国家把这种关系变成一项带有法律后果的登记事实。

intro.en: Marriage reaches English through Old French mariage from Latin maritare 'to wed', a verb built on maritus 'husband'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: marriage 经古法语 mariage 来自拉丁 maritare「使成婚」，该动词由 maritus「丈夫」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Maritus meant 'husband, married man', with the feminine marita 'wife'. Its deeper origin is uncertain: the link to mas 'male' is often proposed but not demonstrated.
items.cn: maritus 意为「丈夫、已婚男子」，阴性形式为 marita「妻子」。其更深来源不确定：把它与 mas「男性」联系起来是常见假说，但未获证实。

items.en: Maritare meant 'to wed, to give in marriage', and was also used of joining a vine to a supporting tree, an image of two lives bound together.
items.cn: maritare 意为「使成婚、嫁娶」，也用于把葡萄藤接到支撑的树上，暗含两条生命被绑在一起。

items.en: Old French mariage named both the wedded state and the wedding feast, and carried both senses into English in the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 mariage 同时指已婚状态与婚宴，并在十三世纪把这两个义项带入英语。

items.en: English marriage kept the double sense from the start, so the same word names the relation and the day that begins it.
items.cn: 英语 marriage 从一开始就保留双重含义，同一个词既指关系，也指开启关系的那一天。

items.en: Canon law made marriage one of the sacraments, while civil law made it a contract with property consequences; both uses shaped the modern word.
items.cn: 教会法把婚姻列为圣事之一，世俗法则把它变成带有财产后果的契约；两种用法共同塑造了现代词义。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): no convincing Latin derivation of maritus has been established, and the recorded first uses of the card-game sense are not fixed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：maritus 尚无令人信服的拉丁派生来源；纸牌游戏义的最早书证年代也不固定。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same Latin stock; group two holds near synonyms for the union or the event.
note.cn: 第一组是同出这一拉丁词干的词；第二组是表示结合或仪式的近义词。

entries.definition: To take as a spouse or to join two people as spouses; marriage is the resulting state or event.
entries.definitionCN: 指娶、嫁或为两人证婚；marriage 是由此形成的状态或事件。

entries.definition: Of or relating to marriage, used in legal and medical contexts rather than in everyday talk.
entries.definitionCN: 指与婚姻有关的形容词，多用于法律与医学语境，而非日常口语。

entries.definition: A formal or religious word for the married state, felt as more solemn than marriage.
entries.definitionCN: 指已婚状态正式或宗教性的说法，比 marriage 更显庄重。

entries.definition: An old borrowing of the same French word, later displaced by marriage; it survives only in historical writing.
entries.definitionCN: 同一法语词的古老借形，后来被 marriage 取代，只在历史文献中留存。

entries.definition: The ceremony and its celebration, without saying anything about the years that follow.
entries.definitionCN: 只指仪式及其庆祝，不涉及婚后的岁月。

entries.definition: A general word for two things becoming one, used of states, trade bodies and couples alike.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指两物合而为一，国家、工会与伴侣都可使用。

entries.definition: A formal, often journalistic word for a wedding, always plural and slightly ornamental.
entries.definitionCN: 指婚礼的正式用语，常见于报道，总是复数且略带修饰色彩。

entries.definition: A lasting arrangement between two people or firms; it makes no claim about vows or law.
entries.definitionCN: 指两人或两家公司之间的长期安排，不涉及誓言或法律。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real word partnerships and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: maritus meant husband, and -age turns the person into the state: the husband-state, then the union.
normal.cn: maritus 指丈夫，-age 把人变成状态：先是「丈夫的身份」，再是婚姻。

normal.en: The family runs marry, marriage, marital, premarital, extramarital and marriageable.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 marry、marriage、marital、premarital、extramarital 与 marriageable。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: arranged marriage, marriage vows, marriage license, marriage of convenience.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：包办婚姻、结婚誓言、结婚证书、权宜婚姻。

normal.en: The metaphor is alive in phrases like a marriage of flavours or a marriage of styles.
normal.cn: 比喻义仍活跃，如风味的结合、风格的结合。

normal.en: The card game sense survives in regional play and in dictionaries, not in general speech.
normal.cn: 纸牌义仍留在地方玩法与词典中，日常口语已不常用。

abstract.en: Picture two streams meeting and then sharing one bed.
abstract.cn: 想象两条溪流汇合后共用一条河床。

abstract.en: Picture a knot tied in public and carried privately for years.
abstract.cn: 想象一个当众打好的结，被私人携带多年。

abstract.en: Picture a vine grafted onto a tree so that both keep growing.
abstract.cn: 想象一根藤接到树上，两者都继续生长。

examples.en: The law recognizes a marriage only after both parties sign the register.
examples.cn: 法律只有在双方签署登记簿后才承认婚姻。

examples.en: Their marriage survived drought, debt and two long separations.
examples.cn: 他们的婚姻熬过了干旱、债务与两次长期分离。

examples.en: Critics called the novel a marriage of detective plot and family saga.
examples.cn: 评论家称这部小说是侦探情节与家族史诗的结合。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「marry（结婚）+ age（年龄）」——到了年纪就结婚

root: 拉丁 maritus「丈夫」（阴性 marita「妻子」）→ 动词 maritare「使成婚」→ 古法语 mariage → 英语 marriage。maritus 的更深来源不确定，与 mas「男性」的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one bond: two people are joined, and the joining is then read as an event, a daily state, a social rule, a metaphor, a game, a sacrament, a treaty and a register entry.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个结合展开：两个人被连在一起，这个结合再依次被读作事件、日常状态、社会制度、比喻、游戏、圣事、盟约与登记记录。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two rings set side by side on one sheet of paper, neither complete without the other.
core.cn: 核心意象：两枚戒指并排放在同一张纸上，缺一枚都不成双。

branches.en: THE BOND AND ITS RECORD: the relation comes first, and the register is how a state sees it.
branches.cn: 结合与记录：关系在先，登记则是国家看见它的方式。

branches.en: THE DAY AND THE VOW: a public rite turns a private promise into a recognised union.
branches.cn: 那一天与那誓言：公开仪式把私下承诺变成被承认的结合。

branches.en: THE LONG MIDDLE: most of a marriage is neither the wedding nor the law but ordinary duration.
branches.cn: 漫长的中间段：婚姻的大部分既不是婚礼也不是法律，而是平常的持续。

branches.en: RULES AND ALLIANCES: a group can define the form, and families can use it as a treaty.
branches.cn: 规则与联盟：群体可以规定形式，家族也可以把它当作条约。

branches.en: TWO BECOME ONE: the metaphor and the card game both play on the matched pair.
branches.cn: 合二为一：比喻义与纸牌义都借成对之物做文章。

intro.en: Marriage is a Latin noun stem plus a French ending, and the same stem builds the legal, medical and everyday words around it.
intro.cn: marriage 由一个拉丁名词词干加一个法语词尾构成，同一词干还构成它周围的法律、医学与日常用词。

latinIntro.en: Latin maritus and marita sit behind marriage, marry and marital; the ending -age names a state or a collection.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 maritus 与 marita 是 marriage、marry 与 marital 的来源；词尾 -age 表状态或集合。

items.example: Maritus supplied the whole family of words.
items.exampleCN: maritus 提供了整个词族的来源。

items.example: The feminine form fills out the pair.
items.exampleCN: 阴性形式补全了这一对。

items.structure: maritare, maritavi, maritatum (Latin verb, first conjugation)
items.example: The verb could also mean to join a vine to a tree.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词也可指把藤接到树上。

items.example: The suffix turns the act of wedding into a lasting state.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把成婚之举变成持续状态。

items.example: Old French kept both senses in one word.
items.exampleCN: 古法语用一个词保留了这两个义项。

items.example: English kept the double sense intact.
items.exampleCN: 英语完整保留了这双重含义。

items.example: Marry is the verb behind the noun.
items.exampleCN: marry 是名词背后的动词。

items.meaning: relating to a husband or to marriage
items.example: Marital law speaks of duties between spouses.
items.exampleCN: 婚姻法讲的是配偶之间的义务。

items.example: Premarital agreements are signed before the wedding.
items.exampleCN: 婚前协议在婚礼之前签署。

definition_zh: 结婚；嫁；娶；为……主持婚礼；使紧密结合
definition_en: to become someone's husband or wife, to take a particular person as a spouse, to conduct a wedding ceremony for a couple, or to join two things closely together
core_image: 两个人把各自的一只手放进同一只手里，一条线从此牵住两端
scene: 秋天的礼堂门口，两家人并肩站着，等那扇木门打开。Her grandmother married a fisherman from the next village in the spring of that hard year.
sceneCN: 这里 marry 是「嫁、娶」，指与某人结成夫妻（第 1 个义项：两个人成为丈夫与妻子）；句意为那年艰难岁月的春天，她的祖母嫁给了邻村的一位渔民。图中可辨识物件：礼堂木门、并肩的两家人、等候的人群。

pos.zh: 结婚；嫁；娶；为……主持婚礼；使紧密结合

collocations.zh: 把技巧与耐心结合起来

derivatives.zh: 由古法语 mariage 而来，与 marry 同出一源，义为「婚姻；婚礼」
出自拉丁语 maritalis（婚姻的），与 marry 同源，义为「婚姻的；夫妻的」
由 marriage 加表示「可以……的」后缀 -able 构成，义为「到了可以结婚的年龄的」
由表示否定的前缀 un- 加 married 构成，义为「未婚的」

senses.title: To become husband and wife
senses.definition: to become the husband or wife of another person, or to have a wedding with someone
senses.definitionCN: 与另一个人成为夫妻，或与某人举行婚礼
senses.example: They married in a small church near the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在一座靠海的小教堂里结了婚。
senses.why: Latin maritus named a married man and maritare named the act of taking a spouse, so the verb begins as the name of a public bond, not of a private feeling.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 maritus 指已婚的男子，动词 maritare 指娶妻或嫁人，所以这个词从一开始就是那层公开缔结的关系的名字，而不是某种私人心情。

senses.title: To take a particular person as a spouse
senses.definition: to take someone as your husband or wife, used when the partner is named as the object
senses.definitionCN: 把某个人娶为妻或嫁为夫，通常把配偶直接放在动词后面
senses.example: She married a fisherman who had never left the bay.
senses.exampleCN: 她嫁给了一个从未离开过这片海湾的渔民。
senses.why: Because the partner is the direct object, English can say who was chosen; that is why it says marry someone and not marry with someone, unlike many European languages.
senses.whyCN: 因为配偶直接做了宾语，英语就能说出被选中的人是谁；所以它说 marry someone，而不像许多欧洲语言那样加一个表示「和」的介词。

senses.title: To conduct a wedding ceremony
senses.definition: of a priest, registrar or other official, to perform the ceremony that makes two people husband and wife
senses.definitionCN: 指神职人员、登记官员或别的主持人举行仪式，使两个人成为夫妻
senses.example: The old priest had married half the couples in that valley.
senses.exampleCN: 那位老神父为山谷里半数的新人主持过婚礼。
senses.why: The same verb serves the couple and the person who declares them married, because a wedding needs an authorized voice to announce that the bond is now in force.
senses.whyCN: 同一个动词既用于新人，也用于那个宣布他们成婚的人，因为婚礼需要一把被授权的嗓子说出这层关系已经生效。

senses.title: To join two things closely
senses.titleCN: 使紧密结合；使融为一体
senses.definition: to bring two things together so that they work as a single whole, said of ideas, skills or flavours
senses.definitionCN: 把两样东西凑在一起，使它们像一体那样运作，多用于想法、技艺或味道
senses.example: The chef marries smoke and citrus in a single spoonful.
senses.exampleCN: 这位厨师把烟熏味与柑橘味融进同一勺里。
senses.why: A marriage is a lasting union, so the verb stretches that image to anything deliberately put into a lasting pair, from a sauce to two crafts practised together.
senses.whyCN: 婚姻是一种长久的联合，于是这个动词把这幅画面推到任何被有意配成一对的东西上，从一味酱汁到两门一起做的手艺。

intro.en: Marry came into English from Old French in the thirteenth century, and behind it stands a Latin word for a married man; the word has always been about a bond made in public, not about romance.
intro.cn: marry 在十三世纪经古法语进入英语，背后是拉丁语里表示「已婚男子」的词；它从出现起讲的就是公开缔结的关系，而不是浪漫。

items.en: Maritus was the ordinary Latin noun for a husband and could also be an adjective for what belongs to a married man; it supplied the base of the verb.
items.cn: maritus 是拉丁语里表示丈夫的普通名词，也可作形容词指属于已婚男子的，并成为那个动词的词基。

items.en: Maritare meant to give a woman in marriage or to take a spouse, and it treated the wedding as a legal and social act rather than a mood.
items.cn: maritare 意为把女子嫁出或娶一位配偶，它把婚礼当作一件法律与社会的行为，而不是一种情绪。

items.en: Old French marier carried the same sense and supplied the form English borrowed, and its noun mariage came along with it.
items.cn: 古法语 marier 保留同样的意思，提供了英语借入的词形，名词 mariage 也随着一起传来。

items.en: Spellings such as marien and maryen settled into marry, and the verb took both the partner and the officiating priest as its object.
items.cn: marien、maryen 这类拼写后来固定为 marry，动词的宾语既可以是配偶，也可以是主持婚礼的神职人员。

items.en: Modern English keeps the wedding sense, allows both marry someone and get married, and stretches the verb to any close pairing such as flavours or skills.
items.cn: 现代英语保留婚礼义，允许 marry someone 与 get married 两种说法，并把动词延伸到任何紧密的配对，例如两种味道或两门技艺。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the wedding family and the Latin words behind it; the near group gathers verbs and nouns for taking a partner or joining two things.
note.cn: 形近组收与婚礼同族的词以及它背后的拉丁词；近义组收表示结为伴侣或把两样东西合起来的动词与名词。

entries.definition: The state or ceremony of being husband and wife, from Old French mariage.
entries.definitionCN: 夫妻的状态或婚礼；出自古法语 mariage，与 marry 同族。

entries.definition: Having a husband or wife, formed from marry with -ed.
entries.definitionCN: 有丈夫或妻子的；已婚的；由 marry 加 -ed 构成。

entries.definition: Relating to marriage or to a husband, from Latin maritalis.
entries.definitionCN: 与婚姻或丈夫有关的；出自拉丁语 maritalis，与 marry 同源。

entries.definition: Not having a husband or wife, formed with the negative prefix un-.
entries.definitionCN: 没有丈夫或妻子的；未婚的；由否定前缀 un- 加 married 构成。

entries.definition: To take someone as a husband or wife, or to perform a wedding; chiefly literary and older use.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人娶为妻或嫁为夫，或主持婚礼；多用于文学与较早的用法。

entries.definition: To marry someone, or to support and adopt a belief; from Latin sponsus, a promised spouse.
entries.definitionCN: 与某人结婚；也指支持并采纳某种主张；出自拉丁语 sponsus（订婚者）。

entries.definition: Two people who are married or in a romantic relationship, or to join two things together.
entries.definitionCN: 已婚或相恋的两个人；也指把两样东西连接起来。

entries.definition: To join two people or things so that they become one.
entries.definitionCN: 把两个人或两样东西结合起来，使它们成为一体。

normalIntro.en: The word is built on a Latin noun for a married man, and its family keeps returning to the wedding, the spouse, and the lasting pair.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在拉丁语表示「已婚男子」的名词上，它的同族词反复回到婚礼、配偶与长久的一对。

normal.en: Latin maritus means a husband, so marry starts as a word about a public bond rather than a private feeling.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 maritus 意为丈夫，所以 marry 起点是一层公开的关系，而不是私人的心情。

normal.en: The verb maritare meant to give a bride or take a spouse, and English borrowed its French descendant marier.
normal.cn: 动词 maritare 意为把新娘嫁出或娶一位配偶，英语借入的是它的法语后代 marier。

normal.en: Because the partner is the direct object, English says marry someone; adding with would make it sound like a ceremony you both merely attend.
normal.cn: 因为配偶是直接宾语，英语说 marry someone；如果加一个表示「和」的介词，听起来就像一场你们只是出席的仪式。

normal.en: The priest who marries a couple uses the same word from the opposite side: he is the one who makes the bond official.
normal.cn: 为一对新人主持婚礼的神父从相反的一侧用同一个词：他是让这层关系正式生效的人。

normal.en: Marriage, marital and married all go back to the same Latin base, one as the noun, one as an adjective of the husband, one as a state.
normal.cn: marriage、marital 与 married 都回到同一个拉丁词基，一个作名词，一个作丈夫的形容词，一个表示所处的状态。

abstract.en: Two hands closing on each other, and the word names the closing, not the warmth that led to it.
abstract.cn: 两只手彼此握住，而这个词命名的是握住本身，不是通向它的那点温热。

abstract.en: A wedding is a sentence said aloud in front of witnesses, and marry is that sentence turned into a verb.
abstract.cn: 婚礼是一句在证人面前说出口的话，而 marry 就是那句话变成的动词。

abstract.en: Once a bond can be made official, it can be made between flavours or skills, and the old public vow quietly becomes a cook's trick.
abstract.cn: 一旦一种结合可以被正式认定，它也能在味道或技艺之间成立，旧日的公开誓言便悄悄变成了厨子的手法。

definition_zh: 奇妙的；了不起的；惊人的；极好的；不可思议的；非凡的
definition_en: extremely good, remarkable, or surprising in a way that fills you with wonder
core_image: 掀开幕布的一瞬，台下有人倒吸一口气：眼前的东西好得不像真的
scene: 观众席安静了一秒，随即爆发出掌声。The audience agreed that the puppet show was simply marvellous.
sceneCN: 这里 marvellous 是「绝妙的、好得令人惊叹」（第 1 个义项：质量极高、令人赞叹）；句意为观众一致认为这场木偶戏实在太精彩了；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 奇妙的；绝妙的；了不起的

derivatives.zh: 同根基础词，经古法语 merveille 进入英语，义为「奇迹；感到惊叹」
由该形容词加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「精彩地；奇妙地」
由该形容词加性质名词后缀 -ness 构成，义为「奇妙；非凡」
固定表达，义为「大自然的奇妙」
动词加介词构成的短语，义为「对……感到惊叹」

senses.title: Extremely good; delightful
senses.definition: so good in quality that you feel pleasure and admiration
senses.definitionCN: 质量好到让人感到愉悦与赞叹
senses.example: We spent a marvellous afternoon by the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在湖边度过了一个极其愉快的下午。
senses.why: What once looked like a miracle is now applied to anything that delights you like a small wonder.
senses.whyCN: 原本指「像奇迹一样」的东西，如今泛指任何像小奇迹一样让你开心的好事。

senses.title: Remarkable; astonishing
senses.definition: so unusual or impressive that it surprises you
senses.definitionCN: 不寻常或令人印象深刻到让你吃惊
senses.example: The bridge is a marvellous feat of engineering.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥是一项了不起的工程壮举。
senses.why: A marvel was something to be wondered at, and achievements beyond expectation keep that sense.
senses.whyCN: marvel 本指「值得惊叹之物」，超出预期的成就保留了这层含义。

senses.title: Seeming almost impossible or magical
senses.titleCN: 奇妙的；近乎不可思议的
senses.definition: appearing so strange or wonderful that it seems hardly real
senses.definitionCN: 显得奇异美妙，几乎不像真实存在
senses.example: The old clock performs a marvellous trick every hour.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老钟每小时都会上演一个奇妙的戏法。
senses.why: The root marvel named things beyond explanation, so the word still carries a faint air of magic.
senses.whyCN: 词根 marvel 本指无法解释的事物，因此这个词至今带一点魔幻气息。

senses.title: Very skilled or impressive in performance
senses.titleCN: 技艺高超的；令人叫绝的
senses.definition: said of a person, voice or skill that works so well it draws praise
senses.definitionCN: 用于形容表现好到引人称赞的人、嗓音或技能
senses.example: She has a marvellous memory for names.
senses.exampleCN: 她记名字的本领令人叫绝。
senses.why: When a human ability seems to work like a wonder, English borrows the word of wonders.
senses.whyCN: 当人的能力好得像奇迹般运转时，英语便借用「奇迹」一族的词来形容。

senses.title: Splendid in appearance or scenery
senses.titleCN: 壮丽多彩的；景色迷人的
senses.definition: strikingly beautiful, said of views, scenes or sights
senses.definitionCN: 美得出众，用于景色、场景或风光
senses.example: From the summit we admired a marvellous sunset.
senses.exampleCN: 在山顶我们欣赏了一场绝美的日落。
senses.why: Scenery that stops the viewer is treated as a wonder shown to the eyes.
senses.whyCN: 让观看者驻足的景色，被当作呈现在眼前的「奇观」。

senses.title: Delightfully amusing or entertaining
senses.definition: amusing or entertaining in a way that gives great pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 有趣好笑，带来极大乐趣
senses.example: He told a marvellous story about his first job.
senses.exampleCN: 他讲了一个关于自己第一份工作的妙趣横生的故事。
senses.why: Pleasure and laughter are close cousins of delight, so good fun also earns the word of wonders.
senses.whyCN: 乐趣与欢笑同「愉悦」是近亲，所以精彩好笑的事也配得上「奇迹」一族的词。

senses.title: Convenient or wonderfully useful
senses.definition: said of a tool, device or arrangement that works remarkably well for you
senses.definitionCN: 用于形容对你来说好用得出奇的工具、装置或安排
senses.example: This little gadget is marvellous for opening jars.
senses.exampleCN: 这个小玩意儿开罐头好用极了。
senses.why: When an object solves a problem almost too well, it is praised as if it were a small miracle.
senses.whyCN: 当一件东西好用到近乎不可思议时，人们便像称赞小奇迹一样称赞它。

senses.title: Said in emphatic agreement or praise
senses.definition: used as an exclamation of strong approval
senses.definitionCN: 用作表示强烈赞许的感叹词
senses.example: Marvellous! The plan is settled, then.
senses.exampleCN: 太好了！那计划就这么定了。
senses.why: Words of wonder easily become cries of joy, so the adjective stands alone in speech.
senses.whyCN: 表惊叹的词很容易变成欢呼，于是这个形容词在口语中可独立成句。

intro.en: Marvellous comes, through Old French merveilleux, from Vulgar Latin *mirabilia 'wonderful things', the plural of Latin mirabilis 'wonderful', from mirari 'to wonder at'. English adopted it in the thirteenth century, and it shares the root with marvel and miracle.
intro.cn: marvellous 经古法语 merveilleux，源自通俗拉丁语 *mirabilia「奇妙之物」，即拉丁 mirabilis「奇妙的」的复数，词根为 mirari「感到惊异」；英语在十三世纪采用，与 marvel、miracle 同根。

items.en: The root *smei is generally reconstructed as meaning 'to smile, to laugh', and wonder was felt as something that makes you open up in delight; this reconstruction is not fully certain.
items.cn: 一般认为印欧词根 *smei 意为「微笑、笑」，惊叹被感受为令人开颜之物；此重构形式并非定论。

items.en: Mirari meant 'to wonder at', mirabilis meant 'wonderful', and its plural *mirabilia named 'wonderful things'.
items.cn: 拉丁 mirari 意为「对……感到惊异」，mirabilis 意为「奇妙的」，其复数 *mirabilia 指「奇妙之物」。

items.en: The word became merveille 'a wonder' and merveilleux 'wonderful', passing into English as marvel and marvellous.
items.cn: 古法语变为 merveille「奇迹」与 merveilleux「奇妙的」，进入英语后成为 marvel 与 marvellous。

items.en: English marvellous first described wonders and strange sights in romance and religious writing, then widened to strong praise of anything excellent.
items.cn: 英语的 marvellous 起初在传奇与宗教文学中形容奇观异事，后扩大为对一切出色事物的强烈赞美。

items.en: British spelling keeps the double l as marvellous, while American spelling simplifies it to marvelous; both come from the same source.
items.cn: 英式拼写保留双写 l 作 marvellous，美式拼写简化为 marvelous；两者同源。

items.en: Today the word mainly means 'extremely good', and its old sense of 'strange, full of wonder' survives in literary style.
items.cn: 如今这个词主要表示「极好的」，旧的「奇异、充满惊叹」之义保留在文学语体中。

note.en: The first group shares the wonder root mirari; the second group holds praise words that differ in strength and flavour.
note.cn: 第一组共享「惊叹」词根 mirari；第二组是表示赞美的词，在强度与色彩上各有不同。

entries.definition: A wonderful thing, or the act of feeling great surprise; the base word of the family.
entries.definitionCN: 令人惊叹的事物，或感到大为惊异；是同族词的基础词。

entries.definition: The American spelling of marvellous, with one l and the same meaning.
entries.definitionCN: marvellous 的美式拼写，只有一个 l，意义相同。

entries.definition: An event believed to be caused by divine power; from Latin mirabilis via Old French.
entries.definitionCN: 被认为由神力造成的奇迹；经古法语源自拉丁 mirabilis。

entries.definition: Like a miracle; said of escapes or recoveries that seem impossible.
entries.definitionCN: 奇迹般的；用于形容看似不可能的脱险或康复。

entries.definition: The adverb form, meaning extremely well or wonderfully.
entries.definitionCN: 副词形式，义为「精彩地；奇妙地」。

entries.definition: Very good or amazing; the most general praise word of the family.
entries.definitionCN: 极好的或令人惊叹的；同族中最通用的赞美词。

entries.definition: Impressive and beautiful; it stresses brilliance rather than wonder.
entries.definitionCN: 出色的、华美的；强调光彩夺目而非惊叹。

entries.definition: Informal for extremely good; originally about fables and legends.
entries.definitionCN: 口语中指「极好的」；原义与寓言、传说相关。

entries.definition: So surprising that it astonishes; it stresses shock more than pleasure.
entries.definitionCN: 令人震惊的；强调惊讶程度多于愉悦。

entries.definition: Worthy of notice because unusual; it stresses being noticed rather than enjoyed.
entries.definitionCN: 不同寻常而值得注意的；强调「引人注意」而非「令人愉悦」。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real derivatives and real fixed phrases, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实派生词与真实固定搭配，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The root is Latin mirari 'to wonder at', shared by marvel, miracle and miraculous.
normal.cn: 词根是拉丁 mirari「感到惊异」，与 marvel、miracle、miraculous 同根。

normal.en: The word came through French merveilleux, so the v and the ending -ous both show French shape.
normal.cn: 此词经法语 merveilleux 传入，所以其中的 v 与词尾 -ous 都是法语印记。

normal.en: The family runs marvel, marvellous, marvellously, marvellousness.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 marvel（奇迹）、marvellous（奇妙的）、marvellously（奇妙地）、marvellousness（奇妙）。

normal.en: British spelling doubles the l; American spelling writes marvelous with one l.
normal.cn: 英式拼写双写 l，美式拼写写作 marvelous，只有一个 l。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark praise: a marvellous opportunity, marvellous news, a marvellous view.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出赞美用法：绝好的机会、极好的消息、奇妙的景色。

abstract.en: Picture a curtain rising on something so good that the whole hall gasps.
abstract.cn: 想象幕布升起，眼前的精彩让全场倒吸一口气。

abstract.en: Picture a traveller telling of sights so strange that listeners marvel rather than doubt.
abstract.cn: 想象旅人讲述奇景，听者只顾惊叹，来不及怀疑。

abstract.en: Picture a small gadget that solves in one click what took an hour before.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小工具，一键解决了从前要花一小时的事。

examples.en: The guide showed us a marvellous hidden valley behind the ridge.
examples.cn: 向导带我们看了山脊后一条奇妙的隐秘山谷。

examples.en: She has done marvellous work with the children's reading club.
examples.cn: 她把孩子们的读书会办得非常出色。

examples.en: It is marvellous that the old bridge survived the flood.
examples.cn: 那座老桥能在洪水中幸存，真是不可思议。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「马窝乐死」——这匹马住进窝棚舒服得乐死了，好得不像话

root: 拉丁 mirari「感到惊异」→ mirabilis「奇妙的」→ 通俗拉丁 *mirabilia「奇妙之物」→ 古法语 merveilleux → 英语 marvellous；同族 marvel、miracle、miraculous。印欧词根 *smei（微笑）为重构形式，存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all grow from one image of wonder: delight in quality, astonishment at achievement, an almost magical strangeness, superb skill, splendid scenery, delightful fun, wonderful usefulness, and a cry of approval.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都从「惊叹」这一个意象生长：对品质的欣喜、对成就的惊叹、近乎魔幻的奇异、高超的技艺、壮丽的景色、妙趣的欢乐、好用得出奇，以及一声赞叹。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a curtain rises, and what appears is so good or so strange that viewers can only marvel.
core.cn: 核心意象：幕布升起，眼前的景象好得或奇得让人只能惊叹。

branches.en: THE DELIGHT FORM: things so pleasant that you feel joy rather than mere approval.
branches.cn: 愉悦形态：让人心生欢喜而不仅是认可的事物。

branches.en: THE ACHIEVEMENT FORM: works and skills so impressive that they astonish.
branches.cn: 成就形态：令人惊叹的出色成果与技艺。

branches.en: THE STRANGENESS FORM: things so odd and lovely that they seem unreal.
branches.cn: 奇异形态：奇异美妙到近乎不真实的事物。

branches.en: THE OBJECT FORM: splendid views and wonderfully useful things.
branches.cn: 对象形态：壮丽的景色与好用得出奇的东西。

branches.en: THE SPOKEN FORM: the word alone, as a cry of strong approval.
branches.cn: 口语形态：单词独立成句，化作一声赞叹。

intro.en: Marvellous rests on Latin mirari 'to wonder at' and the French-derived ending -ous; English adds endings for manner, state and the verb of wondering.
intro.cn: marvellous 建立在拉丁 mirari「感到惊异」与源自法语的词尾 -ous 之上；英语再加表示方式、状态与惊叹动作的词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin mirari 'to wonder at' gives the family: mirabilis 'wonderful', *mirabilia 'wonderful things', and through French the noun marvel and the adjective marvellous.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 mirari「感到惊异」孕育整个词族：mirabilis「奇妙的」、*mirabilia「奇妙之物」，经法语得到名词 marvel 与形容词 marvellous。

items.meaning: to wonder at; to be astonished
items.example: The verb is the root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词是整个词族的根源。

items.example: The adjective also gave English miracle via French.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词经法语也给出英语 miracle。

items.meaning: full of; having the quality of
items.example: The ending turns the noun marvel into a describing word.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把名词 marvel 变成描述词。

items.example: The noun passed into English as marvel.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词进入英语后成为 marvel。

items.example: This is the direct source of the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这是英语形容词的直接来源。

items.meaning: a wonder; to feel great surprise
items.example: The noun and verb kept the older, stronger sense.
items.exampleCN: 名词与动词保留了更古老更强的义项。

items.example: The suffix gives the degree adverb marvellously.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀给出程度副词 marvellously。

items.example: The suffix names the state of being wonderful.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀命名「奇妙」的状态。

items.example: The adverb modifies verbs of performing and working.
items.exampleCN: 这个副词修饰「表现」「起作用」类动词。

items.example: The noun appears in literary description.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词出现在文学描写中。

definition_zh: 团块；大量、大批；质量；群众、大众；弥撒；聚集、集结
definition_en: a large shapeless body of matter, a great quantity of it, or the amount of matter in a body
core_image: 一盆揉好的面团被两只手按下去，整团摊在案板上，越揉越沉
scene: 面粉加水和成一大团，摊在案板上占了半张台面，两只手按下去要费点力。A mass of dough filled the whole board.
sceneCN: 这里 mass 指没有定形、聚成整体的一大团东西（第 1 个义项：不分形状的团块）；句意：一大团面团占满了整块案板。图中可辨识物件：面团、案板、面粉袋、擀面杖；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 团块；大量；质量；群众；弥撒
