definition_zh: 物质；事情；问题；要紧、有关系；【医】脓液
definition_en: the physical stuff that things are made of, an affair under discussion, or to be important
core_image: 一块被雨水泡软的黑泥，手指一捏就能变形，也能弄脏任何碰到它的东西
scene: 泥地刚被雨水浸透，脚一踩就陷下去，鞋底带起黏稠的一团。The sticky mud is the matter that stains every boot in the yard.
sceneCN: 这里 matter 指构成物体的有形之物（第 1 个义项：与形式相对、可被感官触及的实体材料）；句意：那团黏泥就是弄脏院子里每只靴子的物质。图中可辨识物件：泥洼、沾泥的靴子、铁锹、水桶；对应第 1 个义项。

forms.label: 单数（物质义通常不可数）

derivatives.zh: 就事论事的；不动声色的（由本词与「事实」一词构成的复合形容词）
反物质（加表示「相反」的前缀构成，指电荷相反的物质）
无实质内容的（加表示「没有」的后缀构成）
含脓的（加形容词后缀构成，旧医学用法，现已罕用）

senses.title: Physical substance
senses.definition: the physical substance that occupies space and can be seen or touched
senses.definitionCN: 占据空间、可被看见或摸到的实体材料
senses.example: The sticky mud is the matter that stains every boot in the yard.
senses.exampleCN: 那团黏泥就是弄脏院子里每只靴子的物质。
senses.why: matter goes back to Latin materia, which meant timber and the stuff a thing is built from, so the physical sense is the oldest layer.
senses.whyCN: matter 上溯到拉丁 materia，本指木料与造物所用的料，因此「有形之物」是最古老的一层意思。

senses.title: An affair or business
senses.titleCN: 一件待办或已办的事情
senses.definition: a situation, event or piece of business that someone deals with
senses.definitionCN: 某人需要处理的情境、事件或事务
senses.example: She settled a few private matters before leaving for the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 去海边之前，她先处理了几件私事。
senses.why: Latin materia also named the subject under discussion, so the stuff of a talk became the affair itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 materia 也指谈论的题目，于是「谈话的料」就变成了「事情本身」。

senses.title: A problem to be solved
senses.titleCN: 出了差错、需要弄清的问题
senses.definition: a trouble or difficulty, especially one whose cause is not yet known
senses.definitionCN: 麻烦或困难，尤指原因尚未查明的那一种
senses.example: The mechanic asked what the matter was with the engine.
senses.exampleCN: 修理工问发动机出了什么毛病。
senses.why: an affair that has gone wrong is still an affair, so the same word shifted from business to trouble.
senses.whyCN: 出了岔子的事情仍然是一件事情，这个词便从「事务」滑到「麻烦」。

senses.title: To be important
senses.definition: to be of importance or consequence to someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 对某人或某事具有重要性或后果
senses.example: Accuracy matters more than speed in this laboratory.
senses.exampleCN: 在这间实验室里，准确比速度更要紧。
senses.why: what has substance has weight, and English turned that picture into the verb sense of counting for something.
senses.whyCN: 有实体就有分量，英语把这个画面变成了「算得上数」的动词义。

senses.title: The topic of a text or talk
senses.definition: the subject or content that a piece of writing, speech or study is about
senses.definitionCN: 一篇文章、一段讲话或一项研究所谈论的主题与内容
senses.example: The matter of the lecture was soil chemistry in dry regions.
senses.exampleCN: 那场讲座的主题是干旱地区的土壤化学。
senses.why: the material of a text is what it carries, and that carrying sense became the topic it treats.
senses.whyCN: 文章的「料」就是它所承载的东西，这一承载义再转为它所处理的主题。

senses.title: Grounds for concern
senses.titleCN: 值得忧虑或申诉的根据
senses.definition: a reason or grounds for a feeling, claim or action
senses.definitionCN: 某种情绪、主张或行动的根据与理由
senses.example: The inspectors found matter for concern in the water samples.
senses.exampleCN: 检查人员在采水样中发现了值得忧虑的情况。
senses.why: a matter is something that exists and can be pointed at, so it came to mean a fact solid enough to base a claim on.
senses.whyCN: 事情是存在且指得出的事物，于是引申为「站得住脚、可作依据的事实」。

senses.title: Pus from a wound
senses.definition: the fluid that forms in an infected wound, formerly called matter
senses.definitionCN: 感染伤口中生成的液体，旧时称作 matter
senses.example: The old surgical notes describe the wound discharging matter.
senses.exampleCN: 旧时的手术记录描述伤口流出脓液。
senses.why: early medicine used matter for any fluid substance of the body, and pus was simply the matter a wound produced.
senses.whyCN: 早期医学用 matter 泛指体内各种液体，脓不过是伤口生成的「物质」。

senses.title: Content as opposed to form
senses.titleCN: 与形式相对的实质内容
senses.definition: the substantive content of a work, as distinct from its style or outward form
senses.definitionCN: 作品的实际内容，与风格或外在形式相对
senses.example: The matter of the essay outweighs its elegant phrasing.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇随笔的内容比它漂亮的措辞更有分量。
senses.why: philosophy opposed matter to form, and literary criticism then asked whether a work had matter behind its shape.
senses.whyCN: 哲学把「质料」与「形式」对举，文学批评随后追问一部作品在形之外有没有实质。

intro.en: Matter came into English through Old French from Latin materia 'timber, stuff, subject'. The common claim that materia derives from mater 'mother' is a hypothesis, not a settled derivation.
intro.cn: matter 经古法语来自拉丁 materia「木料、材料、题目」。常有人说 materia 由 mater「母亲」派生，那是假说，并非已定的词源。

items.en: Materia meant timber and the material a thing is made from, and by extension the subject of a discussion.
items.cn: materia 指木料以及造物所用的材料，引申为谈论的题目。

items.en: A widely repeated suggestion links materia to mater 'mother', as if the stuff were the mother of the object; this remains a hypothesis and is not established.
items.cn: 一种广为流传的说法把 materia 与 mater「母亲」联系起来，仿佛材料是器物的母亲；这仍属假说，未获证实。

items.en: Old French matere carried both the physical sense and the sense of a subject or affair into English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语 matere 在诺曼时期之后把「物质」与「题目、事务」两义一并带入英语。

items.en: Middle English matter already covered stuff, a business, a question and grounds for complaint, so the wide sense range is old, not modern.
items.cn: 中古英语的 matter 已兼指物质、事务、问题与申诉的理由，可见义域之宽古已有之，并非现代才有。

items.en: Medical writing of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries used matter for bodily fluid and especially for pus, a use that has since narrowed.
items.cn: 十六、十七世纪的医学文献用 matter 指体液，尤指脓，这一用法后来收窄。

items.en: The first recorded dates for several senses are approximate; the word itself is well attested from the thirteenth century.
items.cn: 若干义项的最早记录年代为约数；这个词本身在十三世纪已有充分书证。

note.en: The first group contains forms that look or sound close to matter but may sit on a different root; the second group contains words that share part of its meaning.
note.cn: 第一组是形或音与 matter 接近、但未必同源的词；第二组是与之部分同义的词。

entries.definition: Built on Latin materialis from materia, so it is the adjective and noun grown from the same stock as matter, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 由拉丁 materialis 构成，而 materialis 出自 materia，因此它是与 matter 同出一源的名词与形容词，并非另一个词根。

entries.definition: A French-shaped doublet of material, borrowed later for military equipment and supplies; it shares the Latin source but not the everyday meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 是 material 的法语式借形词，后借入指军用装备与物资；与 material 同源，但日常义不同。

entries.definition: From Latin mater 'mother' through maternellus; it is related to mater, and only through the unproven mater-materia hypothesis could it be called a cousin of matter.
entries.definitionCN: 经 maternellus 出自拉丁 mater「母亲」；它与 mater 有关，只有借助尚未证实的「母亲—材料」假说，才能算作 matter 的远亲。

entries.definition: From Latin matrix 'womb, mould', built on mater; it names a mould or grid, and does not descend from materia.
entries.definitionCN: 出自拉丁 matrix「子宫、模具」，由 mater 构成；它指模具或网格，并非由 materia 传下。

entries.definition: Physical stuff considered as what stands under qualities; matter stresses the material, substance stresses independent existence.
entries.definitionCN: 把物质看作承载属性的基底；matter 强调材料，substance 强调独立存在。

entries.definition: A matter of business or public concern; it covers only the affair sense and never the physical one.
entries.definitionCN: 指事务或公众关注之事；只覆盖「事务」义，绝不指物质。

entries.definition: A topic on which people disagree; it is narrower than matter because it always implies debate.
entries.definitionCN: 指人们有分歧的议题；比 matter 窄，因为它总含争辩之意。

entries.definition: The everyday word for unspecified material; matter is its neutral and technical counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 指未指明材料的日常说法；matter 是它中性、技术化的对应词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real Latin source, the real word family and real fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的拉丁来源、真实的同族词与真实的固定搭配。

normal.en: Latin materia first meant timber, so matter is the stuff a thing is built from.
normal.cn: 拉丁 materia 最初指木料，因此 matter 就是造物所用的料。

normal.en: The family runs matter, material, materially, immaterial and materialize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 matter、material、materially、immaterial 与 materialize。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the affair sense: a matter of time, as a matter of fact, no matter what.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出「事情」义：只是时间问题、事实上、无论发生什么。

normal.en: Subject matter keeps the topic sense visible in publishing and teaching.
normal.cn: 「主题素材」这一说法让「主题」义在出版与教学里一直可见。

normal.en: The verb is used in questions of value: it matters, it does not matter.
normal.cn: 动词义出现在价值判断里：这要紧、这不要紧。

abstract.en: Picture a lump of clay that takes the shape of whatever presses into it.
abstract.cn: 想象一团黏土，什么按上去就留下什么形状。

abstract.en: Picture a desk with one folded note on it, and everyone asks about that note first.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上只有一张折起的字条，所有人先问的都是那张字条。

abstract.en: Picture a scale where the pan with real goods sinks and the empty pan rises.
abstract.cn: 想象一杆秤，装了实物的那端沉下去，空的那端翘起来。

examples.en: In legal drafting, the matter of a contract means its operative content rather than its layout.
examples.cn: 在法律起草中，合同的 matter 指其有效内容，而不是排版。

examples.en: Dark matter does not emit light, yet its gravity holds galaxies together.
examples.cn: 暗物质不发光，但它的引力把星系维系在一起。

examples.en: It does not matter how slowly you go as long as the measurements stay exact.
examples.cn: 只要测量保持精确，你走得多慢都不要紧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「妈特」——妈妈特别在意的那件事，就是要紧的事 → 事情、要紧；妈妈捏的那团泥，就是物质

root: 拉丁 materia「木料、材料、题目」（一说由 mater「母亲」派生，仅为常见假说）→ 古法语 matere「材料、事务」→ 英语 matter；「问题」与「脓」义由「事情」「体内物质」再引申。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses radiate from one lump of stuff: it is the material of things, then the material of talk, then the affair, the trouble inside it, the fact that carries weight, the topic of a text, the fluid in a wound, and finally content set against form.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从同一团「料」辐射出去：先是造物的材料，再是谈话的材料，继而成为事情、事情里的麻烦、有分量的事实、文本的主题、伤口的液体，最后是与形式相对的实质内容。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lump of wet clay that can be shaped, weighed and pointed at.
core.cn: 核心意象：一团湿黏土，可被塑形、称重、指认。

branches.en: THE LUMP ITSELF: clay in the yard and pus in a wound are both stuff a body or a boot meets.
branches.cn: 这团东西本身：院里的泥与伤口的脓，都是身体或靴子会碰到的实体。

branches.en: THE AFFAIR AND ITS SNAG: business first, then the trouble discovered inside it.
branches.cn: 事情与其中的疙瘩：先是事务，再是事务里查出的麻烦。

branches.en: WEIGHT THAT COUNTS: what has substance can tip a decision, so matter becomes a verb.
branches.cn: 有分量才算数：有实体就能压动决定，于是 matter 变成动词。

branches.en: STUFF POINTED AT: the material of a text turns into its topic, and a solid fact into grounds.
branches.cn: 被指认的料：文本的材料变成主题，扎实的事实变成依据。

branches.en: CONTENT AGAINST FORM: philosophy keeps the lump as what remains when style is stripped away.
branches.cn: 内容对形式：哲学把那团料保留为剥去风格后剩下的东西。

intro.en: Matter is built on a Latin root that also yields material and immaterial, so the family can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: matter 建立在一个拉丁词根上，同一词根还生出 material 与 immaterial，因此这个词族可以按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin materia supplies matter, material and materialis; mater supplies maternal and matrix, with the materia link remaining a hypothesis.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 materia 衍生 matter 与 material 一系；mater 衍生 maternal 与 matrix 一系，而 materia 与 mater 的联系仍属假说。

items.example: The root gives the picture of stuff a thing is built from.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根给出「造物所用之料」的画面。

items.example: Its link to materia is a hypothesis, not a proven derivation.
items.exampleCN: 它与 materia 的联系只是假说，并非已证的派生。

items.example: The adjective suffix turns stuff into a describing word.
items.exampleCN: 形容词后缀把「料」变成描述性的词。

items.example: Material keeps both the physical and the serious sense.
items.exampleCN: material 兼有「物质」与「重要」两义。

items.example: It also shapes editorial and commercial.
items.exampleCN: 它同样构成 editorial 与 commercial。

items.example: The negation covers both the physical and the serious sense.
items.exampleCN: 否定前缀同时否掉「物质」与「重要」两义。

items.example: The plan materialized as a real building.
items.exampleCN: 计划落实成了一座真实的建筑。

items.example: The later borrowing narrowed to army supplies.
items.exampleCN: 后借入的这一形收窄为军队物资。

definition_zh: 最大值；最大量；上限；最大的；最高的；（数学）极大值
definition_en: the greatest amount, size, or level that is possible, allowed, or recorded, also used before a noun for the greatest of its kind
core_image: 一根标尺顶到最后一格，指针再也推不上去
scene: 测试台上，工程师把发动机转速一点点推高，仪表的指针最后停在再往上就会报警的那一格。The engine was running at maximum speed when the warning light came on.
sceneCN: 这里 maximum 是「最大值、上限」（第 1 个义项：可以达到的最大量）；句意为报警灯亮起时，发动机正以最高转速运转。图中可辨识物件：测试台、仪表盘、红色指针。

pos.zh: 最大值；最大量；上限；极大值
最大的；最高的；最大限度的

derivatives.zh: 由 maximum 的词干 max- 加 -al 构成，义为「最大的；达到极限的」
由 max- 加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「使最大化」
由 maximize 加名词后缀 -ation 构成，义为「最大化」
由 maximal 加 -ly 构成，义为「最大限度地」

senses.title: The greatest amount or level allowed
senses.definition: the greatest amount, size, or level that is possible, allowed, or recorded
senses.definitionCN: 可能达到、被允许或记录到的最大数量、规模或水平
senses.example: The tank holds a maximum of fifty litres.
senses.exampleCN: 这个油箱最多装五十升。
senses.why: Latin maximus already means greatest, so the noun names the top value of a scale rather than a thing you can touch.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 maximus 本义就是「最大的」，所以这个名词直接指刻度上的顶端数值，而不是能够摸到的实物。

senses.title: The greatest of its kind
senses.definition: used before a noun to describe the greatest size, speed, or level that is allowed or reached
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词前，描述被允许或达到的最大规模、速度或水平
senses.example: The car's maximum load is printed on the door.
senses.exampleCN: 这辆车的最大载重印在车门上。
senses.why: Because maximus is a superlative, the word can stand before a noun and mark that noun as the top of its scale.
senses.whyCN: 因为 maximus 是最高级形式，这个词便能放在名词前，把这个名词标在它那一量级的顶端。

senses.title: The highest point reached in a process
senses.definition: the highest point that a changing quantity reaches before it falls again
senses.definitionCN: 一个变化的量在回落之前所达到的最高点
senses.example: Demand for water reaches its maximum in midsummer.
senses.exampleCN: 对水的需求在盛夏达到峰值。
senses.why: Once the top value has a name, it can also name the moment a curve turns over, so the word moves from a limit to a peak in time.
senses.whyCN: 一旦顶端数值有了名字，它也能指曲线转向的那一刻，于是词义从「界限」转到时间上的「峰值」。

senses.title: The largest value of a mathematical function
senses.definition: the largest value of a function, either in a small neighbourhood or over its whole range
senses.definitionCN: 函数在某一小范围内或整个取值范围内的最大取值
senses.example: The curve shows a maximum near the middle of the graph.
senses.exampleCN: 曲线在图的中间附近出现一个极大值。
senses.why: Mathematicians kept the Latin word because a function's top value is literally the greatest number the formula can produce.
senses.whyCN: 数学家保留了这个拉丁词，因为函数的最大取值字面上就是公式能算出的最大数值。

intro.en: Maximum is a Latin superlative borrowed whole into English, so its history is the story of the word for great rising to its highest degree.
intro.cn: maximum 是把拉丁语最高级原样借进英语的词，它的历史就是「大」这个词一步步升到最高程度的故事。

items.en: Magnus meant great or large, and it is the positive degree behind a whole family of size words.
items.cn: magnus 意为「大的、伟大的」，是整族表示大小的词的原级。

items.en: Maximus was the superlative of magnus, literally the greatest, used of persons as well as things.
items.cn: maximus 是 magnus 的最高级，字面就是「最大的」，也曾用来形容人。

items.en: The neuter form maximum named the greatest amount as a thing in itself, a pattern common in Latin technical writing.
items.cn: 中性形式 maximum 把「最大的量」当作独立的东西来指称，这在拉丁学术写作中很常见。

items.en: English took maximum as a learned word of mathematics and natural philosophy, usually paired with minimum.
items.cn: 英语在十七至十八世纪把 maximum 作为数学与自然哲学的学术词引入，通常与 minimum 配对。

items.en: Modern English uses it as both noun and adjective, from engine speed to legal sentences and everyday caps.
items.cn: 现代英语把它同时用作名词和形容词，从发动机转速到法律刑期再到日常上限都用它。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin family of magnus and maximus; the near-meaning group gathers words for the top of a scale.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 magnus 与 maximus 的拉丁词族走；近义组收表示刻度顶端的词。

entries.definition: As great as possible; the adjective built on the same stem.
entries.definitionCN: 尽可能大的；由同一词干构成的形容词。

entries.definition: To make something as great as possible.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物尽可能大；最大化。

entries.definition: The Latin superlative meaning greatest, the direct source of maximum.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语最高级，意为「最大的」，是 maximum 的直接来源。

entries.definition: Size or extent, especially of something large.
entries.definitionCN: 大小；量级，尤指大的事物的规模。

entries.definition: The smallest amount or level that is possible or allowed.
entries.definitionCN: 可能或被允许的最小数量或水平；最小值。

entries.definition: The highest point of a process or period.
entries.definitionCN: 过程或时期中的最高点；峰值。

entries.definition: The upper limit set on an amount or rate.
entries.definitionCN: 为数量或比率设定的上限。

entries.definition: The greatest possible degree of something.
entries.definitionCN: 某事物可能达到的最大程度。

normalIntro.en: The word carries a Latin superlative, so every memory route leads back to a scale with a top rung.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词带着一个拉丁语最高级，所以每条记忆线索都回到「有一格的刻度」这个意象。

normal.en: Maximus is the superlative of magnus, so maximum is literally the greatest degree of great.
normal.cn: maximus 是 magnus 的最高级，所以 maximum 字面上就是「大」的最高程度。

normal.en: The ending -imum is the Latin neuter, which is why maximum can act as a noun for the greatest amount.
normal.cn: 词尾 -imum 是拉丁语中性形式，所以 maximum 能当名词，指最大的量。

normal.en: Maximal, maximize and maximally all keep the max- stem: the top of the scale as adjective, verb and adverb.
normal.cn: maximal、maximize、maximally 都保留 max- 词干，分别把「顶端」做成形容词、动词和副词。

normal.en: Maximum pairs with minimum in technical writing, the two ends of one measuring scale.
normal.cn: maximum 在学术写作里与 minimum 配对，是同一条量尺的两端。

normal.en: A maximum sentence is the longest term a court may impose, which is the same top-of-scale idea in law.
normal.cn: maximum sentence 是法院能判的最长刑期，法律里用的仍是同一个「刻度顶端」的意思。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler whose last mark is painted red: that mark is the maximum.
abstract.cn: 想象一把尺子，最后一格被涂成红色，那一格就是最大值。

abstract.en: A thermometer stops rising at noon and then falls; that stopping point is the peak sense of the word.
abstract.cn: 温度计在正午停止上升然后回落，那个停住的位置就是这个词的峰值义。

abstract.en: Every scale has two ends; maximum is the end you reach when nothing more can be added.
abstract.cn: 每把尺子都有两端，maximum 就是再也加不上去的那一端。

examples.en: The tank holds a maximum of fifty litres.
examples.cn: 这个油箱最多装五十升。

examples.en: The engine was running at maximum speed.
examples.cn: 发动机正以最高转速运转。

examples.en: Demand for water reaches its maximum in midsummer.
examples.cn: 对水的需求在盛夏达到峰值。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「麦克西姆」——把「麦克」一路推到顶格，就是最大值；记住 maximum 是最值里的最高那一格。

root: 拉丁语 magnus（大的）的最高级 maximus，其中性形式 maximum 被英语原样借用；同族词多含 max- 或 magn-，都与「大」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the top of a scale; from that top value the senses split into the adjective use, the peak reached in time, and the mathematical maximum.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是量尺的顶端；从「顶端数值」分出形容词用法、时间上的峰值，以及数学上的极大值。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a needle stopping at the last red mark on a dial, unable to go higher.
core.cn: 核心意象：指针停在表盘最后一格红色刻度上，再往上就推不动了。

branches.en: a fuel gauge pinned at the last mark
branches.cn: 油表指针顶在最后一格

branches.en: a runner's speed curve flattening at the top
branches.cn: 跑者速度曲线在顶端变平

branches.en: a speed limit sign naming the top allowed rate
branches.cn: 限速牌标出允许的最高速率

branches.en: a river cresting at noon and then dropping
branches.cn: 河水在正午涨到最高，随后下落

branches.en: a graph whose curve turns over near the middle
branches.cn: 曲线在图中间附近转向

intro.en: The word is built from a Latin adjective of size, its superlative, and the endings that turn that stem into nouns, adjectives and verbs.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示大小的拉丁形容词、它的最高级，以及把词干变成名词、形容词和动词的几种词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录。

items.exampleCN: magnus 是整族「大」义词的原级。
maximus 是 magnus 的最高级形式。
maximum 是中性形式，可以作名词。
maximum 中的 -imum 是中性词尾。
maximal 由 max- 加 -al 构成。

items.meaning: relating to, having the quality of
items.exampleCN: -al 把 max- 变成形容词 maximal。

items.meaning: to make as great as possible
items.exampleCN: maximize 由 max- 加 -ize 构成动词。

items.meaning: to make or cause to be
items.exampleCN: -ize 把词干变成动词 maximize。

definition_zh: 可以；可能；（表示祝愿）愿；五月
definition_en: a modal verb used to give or ask for permission, to say that something is possible, or to express a wish, and also the name of the fifth month
core_image: 一扇虚掩的门，门缝里透出光，能不能推开还说不准
scene: 会议室的窗外在下雨，主管把文件合上，抬手指了指门口。You may leave the meeting early if the weather gets worse.
sceneCN: 这里 may 是「可以」（第 1 个义项：表示许可）；句意为如果天气变坏，你可以提前离开会议。图中可辨识物件：合上的文件夹、窗上的雨痕、半开的门。

pos.zh: 可以；可能；愿；用于委婉请求

derivatives.zh: may 的历史过去式，也可单独表示「可能」，语气更弱
由 may 与 be 合并而成，义为「也许」
由名词 might（力量）加 -y 构成，义为「强大的」

senses.title: Used to give or ask for permission
senses.definition: used to say that someone is allowed to do something, or to ask politely for permission
senses.definitionCN: 用于表示某人被允许做某事，或礼貌地请求许可
senses.example: You may leave the meeting early if the weather gets worse.
senses.exampleCN: 如果天气变坏，你可以提前离开会议。
senses.why: The Old English verb magan meant to be able, and permission is its everyday result: if you are able and nobody forbids it, you may do it.
senses.whyCN: 古英语动词 magan 意为「有能力」，许可就是它最日常的结果：只要你有能力又无人禁止，你就可以做。

senses.title: Used to say that something is possible
senses.definition: used to say that something is possible but not certain
senses.definitionCN: 用于表示某事有可能，但并不确定
senses.example: She may be late because the trains are slow tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 她可能会迟到，因为今晚列车开得慢。
senses.why: The same sense of being able turns into speculation: a thing that can happen is a thing that may happen.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「有能力」的意思转成推测：能够发生的事，也就是可能发生的事。

senses.title: Used to express a wish or blessing
senses.definition: used at the beginning of a sentence to express a hope or a blessing
senses.definitionCN: 放在句首，用来表达希望或祝福
senses.example: May you both have a long and happy life together.
senses.exampleCN: 愿你们二人白头偕老、生活幸福。
senses.why: A wish is something you want to be able to happen, so Old English put the verb of ability first to voice a blessing.
senses.whyCN: 愿望就是你希望「能够发生」的事，所以古英语把表示「能够」的动词提到句首，用来表达祝福。

senses.title: The fifth month of the year
senses.definition: the fifth month of the year, written with a capital letter
senses.definitionCN: 一年的第五个月，书写时首字母大写
senses.example: May is the month when the garden finally turns green.
senses.exampleCN: 五月是花园终于变绿的那个月份。
senses.why: The month name comes from Latin Maius, named after a Roman goddess; it shares spelling with the modal but not its history.
senses.whyCN: 月份名来自拉丁语 Maius，以罗马女神命名；它与情态动词拼写相同，来历却完全不同。

intro.en: The modal may goes back to an Old English verb of ability, while the month May comes from a Latin god's name; the two only happen to be spelled alike.
intro.cn: 情态动词 may 来自古英语中表示「有能力」的动词，而月份 May 来自拉丁语神名；两者只是碰巧拼写相同。

items.en: A reconstructed root often written meg- or magh- is thought to carry the sense of being able or having power.
items.cn: 一般认为，一个重构词根（常写作 meg- 或 magh-）带有「有能力、有力量」的意思。

items.en: Old English magan meant to be able or to have power, and it was already a defective verb without an ordinary infinitive.
items.cn: 古英语 magan 意为「能够、有力量」，当时已是缺少普通不定式的残缺动词。

items.en: Its present forms ran mæg and magon, and its past was meahte, shapes that survived into modern English.
items.cn: 它的现在时形式有 mæg、magon，过去式是 meahte，这些形式一直活到现代英语。

items.en: Middle English kept may and might, and the pair began to split between present permission and past or tentative possibility.
items.cn: 中古英语保留了 may 与 might，这一对开始分工：前者表现在的许可，后者表过去或委婉的可能。

items.en: Modern English uses may for permission, possibility and blessings, and writes the month May with a capital letter from Latin Maius.
items.cn: 现代英语用 may 表示许可、可能和祝愿；月份 May 首字母大写，来自拉丁语 Maius。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the modal's old forms and compounds; the near-meaning group gathers other ways of saying possible or allowed.
note.cn: 形近组收这个情态动词的旧形式与复合词；近义组收其他表示「可能」或「被允许」的说法。

entries.definition: The historical past tense of may, now also a weaker word for possibility.
entries.definitionCN: may 的历史过去式，如今也单独表示较弱的可能性。

entries.definition: Perhaps; a single word built from may and be.
entries.definitionCN: 也许；由 may 与 be 合并而成的一个词。

entries.definition: The Old English verb meaning to be able, the ancestor of may.
entries.definitionCN: 古英语动词，意为「能够」，是 may 的祖先。

entries.definition: Strong and powerful, built on the noun might meaning strength.
entries.definitionCN: 强大的；由表示力量的名词 might 加后缀构成。

entries.definition: Used for ability or permission, often more direct than may.
entries.definitionCN: 表示能力或许可，通常比 may 直接。

entries.definition: The past of can, and a politer or more tentative form.
entries.definitionCN: can 的过去式，也是更客气、更不确定的说法。

entries.definition: An adverb meaning possibly, close to the speculative use of may.
entries.definitionCN: 副词，意为「也许」，接近 may 的推测用法。

entries.definition: Permitted by a rule or by a person in charge.
entries.definitionCN: 被规则或负责人允许的。

normalIntro.en: The modal is an old verb of ability worn down to three letters, and the month beside it is a Latin name that only looks the same.
normalIntro.cn: 这个情态动词是磨得只剩三个字母的古老「能力」动词，而旁边那个月份只是长得一样的拉丁名字。

normal.en: Magan in Old English meant to be able, so may began as a word about capacity rather than permission.
normal.cn: 古英语 magan 意为「能够」，所以 may 起初是讲能力的词，而不是讲许可的。

normal.en: Its past tense meahte became might, which is why might still sounds like a softer may.
normal.cn: 它的过去式 meahte 变成 might，所以 might 至今听起来像一个语气更软的 may。

normal.en: Maybe is simply may plus be written as one word, a compressed way of saying it may be so.
normal.cn: maybe 就是 may 与 be 合成一个词，是「it may be so」的压缩说法。

normal.en: May well means there is good reason to think so, while may as well means there is no better choice.
normal.cn: may well 意为「有充分理由这样想」，may as well 意为「没有更好的选择」。

normal.en: The month May is capitalized because it is a proper name from Latin Maius, not the modal verb.
normal.cn: 月份 May 首字母大写，因为它是来自拉丁语 Maius 的专名，而不是这个情态动词。

abstract.en: Think of a half-open door: you are able to push it, but whether you should is another question.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇半开的门：你有能力推开，但该不该推是另一回事。

abstract.en: A forecast saying it may rain is a sentence standing between yes and no.
abstract.cn: 预报说可能下雨，就是一句停在「是」与「否」之间的话。

abstract.en: The same letters name a month and a mood of possibility; English lets spelling hide two separate histories.
abstract.cn: 同样的字母既是一个月份，也是一种可能语气；英语就让拼写掩盖了两段不同的来历。

examples.en: You may leave the meeting early if the weather gets worse.
examples.cn: 如果天气变坏，你可以提前离开会议。

examples.en: She may be late because the trains are slow tonight.
examples.cn: 她可能会迟到，因为今晚列车开得慢。

examples.en: May you both have a long and happy life together.
examples.cn: 愿你们二人白头偕老、生活幸福。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「没」——有没有把握说不准，所以 may 是「可能」；问人可不可以，也用 may。

root: 古英语 magan（能够、有力量）的现在式 mæg 演变而来，过去式 meahte 成为 might；月份 May 另出自拉丁语 Maius，与此词没有词源关系。

sensesIntro.en: The core is ability turning into possibility; permission is the everyday side of that ability, the wish is its optative use, and the month is a separate Latin name.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「能力」转为「可能」；许可是这种能力最日常的一面，祝愿是它的祈愿用法，而月份则是另一个拉丁名字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a door standing ajar, able to be pushed but not yet pushed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇虚掩的门，推得开，却还没有推。

branches.en: an open door with a hand resting on the frame
branches.cn: 一扇开着的门，一只手搭在门框上

branches.en: a sky that could rain or could clear
branches.cn: 一片可能下雨也可能放晴的天

branches.en: a sign saying that visitors are permitted
branches.cn: 一块写着访客获准进入的牌子

branches.en: a toast raised at a wedding
branches.cn: 婚礼上举起的一杯酒

branches.en: a garden turning green in the fifth month
branches.cn: 花园在第五个月转绿

intro.en: The word is an Old English verb of ability worn down to three letters, with a compound and a past form built on the same stem.
intro.cn: 这个词是古英语中表示「能够」的动词，磨得只剩三个字母，并用同一词干造出一个复合词和一个过去式。

latinIntro.en: The modal verb has no reliable Latin cognate, since it descends from Old English; only the month name May goes back to Latin Maius.
latinIntro.cn: 这个情态动词没有可靠的拉丁同族词，因为它源自英语本土；只有月份名 May 可上溯到拉丁语 Maius。

items.meaning: to be able, to have power
items.exampleCN: magan 是 may 的古英语原形。

items.meaning: first and third person singular of magan
items.meaningCN: magan 的第一、第三人称单数
items.exampleCN: mæg 是 magan 的现在式单数形式。
meahte 是 magan 的过去式。
-an 标出 magan 的不定式身份。

items.meaningCN: may 的过去式；也可指力量
items.exampleCN: might 由 meahte 演变而来。
may 是磨短之后的现代形式。
maybe 由 may 与 be 合并而成。
be 是 maybe 的后半部分。

latinEntries.meaning: of May, belonging to the month of May

definition_zh: 也许；可能；（口语）或许吧；不确定的事
definition_en: used to say that something is possible but not certain, or to make a gentle suggestion, and informally a thing that is still undecided
core_image: 天平两端各放一枚砝码，还在轻轻摇晃，没有落定
scene: 两个人站在站台上，雨云压得很低，列车时刻牌迟迟不翻。Maybe the rain will stop before we reach the station.
sceneCN: 这里 maybe 是「也许」（第 1 个义项：表示不确定的可能）；句意为也许我们到站之前雨就会停。图中可辨识物件：站台、时刻牌、压低的雨云。

pos.zh: （口语）不确定的事；悬而未决的事

derivatives.zh: maybe 的前半部分，表示「可能」，来自古英语 magan
与 may 同源的历史过去式，也可表示较弱的可能
maybe 的后半部分，来自古英语表示「是、存在」的动词

senses.title: Used to say something is possible but not certain
senses.definition: used when you think something is possible, without saying that it is certain
senses.definitionCN: 在你认为某事有可能、但不确定时使用
senses.example: Maybe the rain will stop before we reach the station.
senses.exampleCN: 也许我们到站之前雨就会停。
senses.why: The word is may plus be: a compressed sentence saying it may be so, with the doubt of may kept inside.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 may 加 be，把一个意为「或许如此」的句子压缩起来，may 那点不确定感也留在里面。

senses.title: Used to make a gentle suggestion
senses.definition: used in speech to suggest a course of action without sounding like an order
senses.definitionCN: 口语中用来提出某个做法，又不像在下命令
senses.example: Maybe we should call her before we drive over.
senses.exampleCN: 也许我们该在开车过去之前给她打个电话。
senses.why: A suggestion phrased with maybe leaves the decision open, so the same doubt becomes a polite way of proposing.
senses.whyCN: 用 maybe 提出的建议把决定权留开，于是同一份不确定就变成了客气地提议。

senses.title: A hesitant answer that agrees without promising
senses.definition: used alone as an answer that neither accepts nor refuses
senses.definitionCN: 单独用作回答，既不答应也不拒绝
senses.example: Will you come to the reunion? Maybe.
senses.exampleCN: 你会来聚会吗？或许吧。
senses.why: Because maybe marks an open possibility, a bare maybe as an answer lets the speaker stay uncommitted.
senses.whyCN: 因为 maybe 标出的是一种开放的可能，单独用它作答，说话人就不必作出承诺。

senses.title: Something that is still undecided
senses.definition: an informal noun for a plan or result that is not settled yet
senses.definitionCN: 非正式的名词，指尚未定下来的计划或结果
senses.example: The trip is still a maybe until the tickets are booked.
senses.exampleCN: 在机票订好之前，这趟旅行还说不准。
senses.why: Once maybe names a possibility, it can be turned into a noun for the thing that sits in that doubtful state.
senses.whyCN: 既然 maybe 指的是一种可能性，它就能被当作名词，指处在那种不确定状态里的事情。

intro.en: Maybe is an English compound rather than a borrowed word: may came from an Old English verb of ability, be from the verb of existence, and the two were written as one word in Middle English.
intro.cn: maybe 是英语本土的复合词，不是借词：may 来自古英语表示「能够」的动词，be 是表示存在的动词，两者在中古英语时期合并成一个词。

items.en: Magan meant to be able, and its present stem supplied may as the word for possibility.
items.cn: magan 意为「能够」，它的现在时词干提供了表示可能性的 may。

items.en: Beon meant to be or to exist, and it is the source of modern be in all its irregular forms.
items.cn: beon 意为「是、存在」，是现代 be 及其各种不规则形式的来源。

items.en: The two words stood side by side as may be, a clause meaning it may be so.
items.cn: 这两个词在中古英语中并排出现，写作 may be，是一个意为「或许如此」的小句。

items.en: By the late medieval period the pair was written as one word and used like an adverb.
items.cn: 到中古英语后期，这一对已被写成一个词，并像副词一样使用。

items.en: Modern English uses maybe freely in speech and informal writing, beside perhaps in more formal styles.
items.cn: 现代英语在口语和非正式写作中自由使用 maybe，较正式文体则常用 perhaps。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the parts and close neighbours of the compound; the near-meaning group collects other adverbs of possibility.
note.cn: 形近组收这个复合词的组成部分与近邻；近义组收其他表示可能性的副词。

entries.definition: The modal verb meaning can or possibly will, the front half of maybe.
entries.definitionCN: 情态动词，意为「可以」或「可能」，是 maybe 的前半部分。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to exist or to be, the back half of maybe.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「是、存在」的动词，是 maybe 的后半部分。

entries.definition: The past form of may, also used for weaker possibility.
entries.definitionCN: may 的过去式，也用来表示较弱的可能性。

entries.definition: A verb phrase meaning it is possible that it is, written as two words.
entries.definitionCN: 动词短语，意为「可能是」，写作两个词。

entries.definition: A more formal adverb for possibility.
entries.definitionCN: 表示可能性的较正式副词。

entries.definition: An adverb saying that something could happen or be true.
entries.definitionCN: 表示某事可能发生或属实的副词。

entries.definition: An adverb saying something is likely, stronger than maybe.
entries.definitionCN: 表示某事很可能，语气比 maybe 强。

entries.definition: Used when you suppose something is true from the evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 根据证据推断某事属实时使用。

normalIntro.en: The word is two short verbs fused, and its meaning is the doubt that may brings to the plain verb be.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由两个短动词熔合而成，意思就是 may 带给 be 的那点不确定。

normal.en: Maybe is may plus be, so the word literally contains the sentence it may be.
normal.cn: maybe 是 may 加 be，字面上就装着「it may be」这句话。

normal.en: May started as an Old English verb of ability, which is why maybe carries possibility rather than certainty.
normal.cn: may 起初是古英语中表示能力的动词，所以 maybe 带的是可能而非确定。

normal.en: Written as two words, may be is a verb phrase; written as one, maybe is an adverb.
normal.cn: 写成两个词时 may be 是动词短语，写成一个词时 maybe 是副词。

normal.en: Maybe not and maybe so are the two easiest pairs to remember, one closing and one opening the possibility.
normal.cn: maybe not 与 maybe so 是最容易记的两对，一个关上一个打开可能性。

normal.en: A big maybe is the informal noun use, for something still undecided.
normal.cn: a big maybe 是它的非正式名词用法，指还悬着的事。

abstract.en: Picture two coins still swinging on a balance, never settling on one side.
abstract.cn: 想象天平上两枚硬币还在晃，始终不落向一边。

abstract.en: Saying maybe is like leaving a door half open so that either answer can walk in.
abstract.cn: 说 maybe 就像把门留半开，让哪个答案都能走进来。

abstract.en: Two short verbs joined into one word show how English compresses a whole hesitant sentence into a few sounds.
abstract.cn: 两个短动词并成一个词，正好显示英语如何把一整句犹豫的话压成很少的音节。

examples.en: Maybe the rain will stop before we reach the station.
examples.cn: 也许我们到站之前雨就会停。

examples.en: Maybe we should call her before we drive over.
examples.cn: 也许我们该在开车过去之前给她打个电话。

examples.en: The trip is still a maybe until the tickets are booked.
examples.cn: 在机票订好之前，这趟旅行还说不准。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「妹比」——妹妹和别人比，谁更好还说不准；记住 maybe 是「也许」。

root: 由古英语 magan（能够）演变来的 may 与古英语 beon（是、存在）演变来的 be 合并而成；中古英语后期写成一词，作副词使用。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an open possibility; from it come the plain adverb, the polite suggestion, the hesitant answer, and the informal noun.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一个开放的可能性；由此分出普通副词用法、客气建议、含糊回答，以及非正式的名词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a balance still swinging, with neither side yet resting on the table.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平还在轻晃，两端都没有落到桌上。

branches.en: a forecast that keeps both options open
branches.cn: 一份把两种可能都留着的天气预报

branches.en: a hand raised before anyone starts driving
branches.cn: 还没发动车子前抬起的一只手

branches.en: a bare maybe given to a question
branches.cn: 对一个问题只回一句「或许吧」

branches.en: a plan sitting on the table without a date
branches.cn: 摊在桌上却没有日期的计划

branches.en: a word that turns doubt into something you can hold
branches.cn: 一个把犹豫变成可以拿在手里的东西的词

intro.en: The word is two Old English verbs welded together, and both pieces still show in the spelling.
intro.cn: 这个词由两个古英语动词焊在一起，两个部件在拼写里仍然看得见。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded for this word, which is an English compound of two Old English verbs.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录，它是由两个古英语动词构成的英语复合词。

may 是 magan 磨短后的现在形式。
beon 是现代 be 的古英语来源。

maybe 由两个词合并而成。

items.meaningCN: be 的一个现在式形式
items.exampleCN: is 是 be 的一个现在式形式。

definition_zh: 我（宾格）；我（作介词宾语）；我（作表语）；我（口语作主语）
definition_en: the pronoun a speaker uses for himself or herself when it is the object of a verb or preposition, and in a few other positions in informal English
core_image: 说话人把手按在自己胸口，向对面的人指一下自己
scene: 雨夜里公交站只剩两个人，陌生人把伞往这边递过来。Could you share the umbrella with me until the bus comes?
sceneCN: 这里是「介词后的宾格」（第 2 个义项：作介词宾语）；句意为能否把伞与我共用到公交车来。图中可辨识物件：雨伞、站牌、湿漉漉的地面。

pos.zh: 我（宾格；口语中也可作主语或表语）

derivatives.zh: 由 me 加 -self 构成的反身代词，义为「我自己」
与 me 同属第一人称代词体系的名词性物主代词，义为「我的东西」
与 me 同源的第一人称物主限定词，义为「我的」

senses.title: The object of a verb
senses.definition: the pronoun a speaker uses when referring to himself or herself as the direct or indirect object of a verb
senses.definitionCN: 说话人指自己、充当动词直接或间接宾语时用的代词
senses.example: The teacher asked me a difficult question.
senses.exampleCN: 老师问了我一个难题。
senses.why: Old English kept a separate accusative form mē for the object role, so the pronoun changes shape the moment it stops being the subject.
senses.whyCN: 古英语为宾语角色保留了独立的宾格形式 mē，所以这个代词一旦不做主语就得换形，me 正是那套格变化留下的宾语形态。

senses.title: The object of a preposition
senses.definition: the pronoun used after a preposition when the speaker is the thing the preposition points to
senses.definitionCN: 介词之后使用、表示介词所指向的说话人本身的代词
senses.example: This letter is addressed to me.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信是寄给我的。
senses.why: Old English prepositions governed the dative, and the same mē served both object cases, which is why one short form now covers every preposition.
senses.whyCN: 古英语的介词支配与格，而同一个 mē 同时承担两种宾语格，所以今天一个短形式就能跟在所有介词后面。

senses.title: The complement after be
senses.definition: the pronoun used after a linking verb or in a comparison, where older grammar once expected the subject form
senses.definitionCN: 连系动词之后或比较句中使用的代词，旧语法在此处本要求用主格
senses.example: It was me at the door, not my brother.
senses.exampleCN: 在门口的是我，不是我弟弟。
senses.why: After be the pronoun is felt as the point of focus rather than the doer, so the object form survives where Latin-based rules would still ask for the subject form.
senses.whyCN: 在 be 之后，代词被感知为被指出的焦点而不是动作发出者，因此在依拉丁规则本该用主格的位置，宾格形式反而留了下来。

senses.title: The subject in informal speech
senses.definition: the pronoun used as part of the subject in casual speech, especially when it is joined to another noun by and
senses.definitionCN: 随意口语中充当主语一部分的代词，尤指与另一个名词用 and 并列时
senses.example: Me and my cousin run a small shop.
senses.exampleCN: 我和我表弟经营一家小店。
senses.why: In relaxed speech the pronoun is treated as one unmarked word rather than as a case form, so me spreads into the subject slot that school grammar reserves for I.
senses.whyCN: 在随意的口语里，代词被当成一个不带格标记的词，于是 me 扩散到学校语法留给 I 的主语位置。

intro.en: Me is the old object form of the first person pronoun, and it descends from a root shared by Latin and English.
intro.cn: me 是第一人称代词古老的宾语形式，其词根为拉丁语与英语所共有。

items.en: A reconstructed first person root *me- supplied the oblique forms of the pronoun in many branches of the family.
items.cn: 重构的第一人称词根 *me- 为这一语族许多分支提供了代词的斜格形式。

items.en: The accusative *mek and the dative *miz stood behind the single Old English form that English later kept.
items.cn: 宾格 *mek 与与格 *miz 共同支撑了古英语那个后来被英语保留下来的单一形式。

items.en: Old English mē served as both accusative and dative of ic, the word for I.
items.cn: 古英语 mē 同时充当 ic（我）的宾格与与格。

items.en: Middle English kept me while the old case system slowly broke down and word order took over the work of marking roles.
items.cn: 中古英语保留了 me，同时旧的格系统逐渐瓦解，标记句子角色的工作转由词序承担。

items.en: Modern English uses me for every object role and, informally, for subjects and complements as well.
items.cn: 现代英语用 me 承担所有宾语角色，口语中还扩展到主语与表语。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the other forms of the same pronoun paradigm; the near-meaning group collects pronouns that also point at a person.
note.cn: 形近组收同一代词体系里的其他形式；近义组收同样指向某个人称的代词。

entries.definition: The subject form of the same first person pronoun.
entries.definitionCN: 同一第一人称代词的主格形式。

entries.definition: The possessive determiner built on the same pronoun stem.
entries.definitionCN: 同一代词词干上的物主限定词。

entries.definition: The possessive pronoun standing for something that belongs to the speaker.
entries.definitionCN: 表示属于说话者之物的物主代词。

entries.definition: The Latin pronoun for me, from the same reconstructed first person root.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁语中表示「我」的宾格代词，出自同一重构的第一人称词根。

entries.definition: The object form of we, used when the speaker is part of a group.
entries.definitionCN: we 的宾格，说话人属于一个群体时使用。

entries.definition: A reflexive pronoun referring back to a general person.
entries.definitionCN: 回指泛指的「自己」的反身代词。

entries.definition: The self as consciously perceived, especially in psychology.
entries.definitionCN: 心理学中自觉意识到的「自我」。

normalIntro.en: The word survives from a pronoun paradigm that once marked case on every form; its nearest relatives are the other first person forms.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词来自一套曾为每个形式标格的代词体系，它最近的亲属就是第一人称的其他形式。

normal.en: Old English had ic for the subject and mē for the object, and English kept the second form as me.
normal.cn: 古英语用 ic 作主语、mē 作宾语，英语把后者留成了 me。

normal.en: The same m- stem runs through my, mine and myself, so all of them point back to the speaker.
normal.cn: 同一个 m- 词干贯穿 my、mine 与 myself，它们都指回说话人。

normal.en: Latin mē is the same pronoun, so the resemblance is not a coincidence but a shared inheritance.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 mē 是同一个代词，所以这种相似不是巧合，而是共同的继承。

normal.en: After a preposition English almost always wants me rather than I, because the object case survived longest there.
normal.cn: 在介词后面英语几乎总是用 me 而不是 I，因为宾格在那里存留得最久。

normal.en: Excuse me is a fixed phrase, so the object form stays even though no verb follows it.
normal.cn: excuse me 是固定短语，所以后面没有动词时也仍然用宾格形式。

abstract.en: Think of me as the version of I that other people can act upon: it appears when something is done to the speaker.
abstract.cn: 把 me 想成可以被别人施加动作的那个 I：当有事情落到说话人身上时，它就出现。

abstract.en: A pronoun is a placeholder, and me is the smallest label a speaker can attach to a body in a room.
abstract.cn: 代词是占位符，而 me 是说话人能贴到房间里某具身体上的最小标签。

abstract.en: A single letter m carries the speaker across languages, from English me to Latin mē.
abstract.cn: 一个字母 m 就把说话人带过语言的边界，从英语 me 到拉丁语 mē。

examples.en: The teacher asked me a difficult question.
examples.cn: 老师问了我一个难题。

examples.en: This parcel is for me, not for my sister.
examples.cn: 这个包裹是给我的，不是给我妹妹的。

examples.en: It was me who forgot the keys.
examples.cn: 忘带钥匙的是我。

definition_zh: 一餐；一顿饭；饭食；粗粉；谷物磨成的粉
definition_en: an occasion when food is eaten, the food served at that occasion, or grain ground into a coarse powder
core_image: 木桌上摆着一只碗和一袋磨好的谷物粉，吃饭与磨粉落在同一幅画面里
scene: 清晨的厨房里，母亲把燕麦倒进锅里，孩子已经坐在桌边等。We usually have a quiet meal before the school bus arrives.
sceneCN: 这里是「一餐、一顿饭」（第 1 个义项：吃饭的场合）；句意为校车到来之前，我们通常安静地吃一顿饭。图中可辨识物件：锅、燕麦、木桌、碗。

derivatives.zh: 由 meal 与 time 复合而成，义为「用餐时间」
由 meal 加形容词后缀 -y 构成，义为「粉状的；发白的」
由 oat 与 meal（粗粉）复合而成，义为「燕麦片」
由 corn 与 meal（粗粉）复合而成，义为「玉米粗粉」

senses.title: An occasion when food is eaten
senses.definition: a fixed or usual occasion on which a person sits down and eats food
senses.definitionCN: 一个人固定或惯常坐下来吃饭的场合
senses.example: We sat down to a quiet meal at seven.
senses.exampleCN: 我们七点坐下来安静地吃了一顿饭。
senses.why: Old English mǣl first meant a measured or appointed time, so a meal was originally the hour set aside for eating rather than the food itself.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 mǣl 本指量好、约定的时间，所以 meal 最初是吃饭被安排的那个时刻，而不是食物本身。

senses.title: The food eaten at such an occasion
senses.definition: the food that is served and eaten at one sitting
senses.definitionCN: 一次坐下用餐时所端上并被吃掉的食物
senses.example: She cooked a simple meal of rice and vegetables.
senses.exampleCN: 她做了一顿简单的米饭加蔬菜。
senses.why: Once the appointed hour had a name, the word slid from the time to what filled that time, namely the food on the table.
senses.whyCN: 一旦那个约定的时刻有了名字，词义就从时间滑向填满这段时间的东西，也就是桌上的食物。

senses.title: Grain ground into coarse powder
senses.definition: grain, especially oats or corn, ground coarsely rather than into fine flour
senses.definitionCN: 尤指燕麦或玉米磨得较粗、而非磨成细面粉的谷物
senses.example: The mill turns oats into meal for the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 磨坊把燕麦磨成粗粉，留着过冬。
senses.why: This sense comes from a different Old English word, melu, meaning flour; the two words fell together in spelling and now share one entry.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项来自另一个古英语词 melu，意为面粉；两个词在拼写上合流，如今共用一个词条。

senses.title: Any coarsely ground product used as feed or fertilizer
senses.definition: a powdered product made by grinding bones, fish or shells, used as animal feed or fertilizer
senses.definitionCN: 把骨头、鱼或贝壳磨成粉、用作饲料或肥料的产品
senses.example: Bone meal is spread on the field before planting.
senses.exampleCN: 种植前把骨粉撒在田里。
senses.why: The grinding image at the heart of the flour sense extends easily to bones, fish and shells once industry needs a word for powdered additives.
senses.whyCN: 面粉义项核心的「磨碎」意象很容易延伸到骨头、鱼和贝壳，只要工业需要一个词来称粉末状的添加物。

intro.en: Meal is two Old English words that look alike today: one for an appointed time, one for ground grain.
intro.cn: meal 其实是两个古英语词，今天看起来一样：一个指约定的时间，一个指磨碎的谷物。

items.en: The noun *mēlą meant a measure or a marked point of time, and it is the ancestor of the repast sense.
items.cn: 名词 *mēlą 意为尺度或标出的时间点，是「一餐」这一义项的祖先。

items.en: Old English mǣl named an appointed time and later the meal eaten at that time.
items.cn: 古英语 mǣl 指约定的时刻，后来也指那个时刻吃的那顿饭。

items.en: A separate word, melu, meant flour or grain ground fine, and it is the ancestor of the powder sense.
items.cn: 另一个词 melu 意为面粉或磨细的谷物，是「粗粉」义项的祖先。

items.en: Middle English spelled both words close to mele, and they gradually merged into one form.
items.cn: 中古英语把两个词都写成接近 mele 的形式，二者逐渐合并成一个词形。

items.en: Modern English keeps both senses in one entry and builds compounds such as oatmeal and cornmeal.
items.cn: 现代英语把两个义项收在同一词条里，并构成 oatmeal、cornmeal 等复合词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the powder family and its mill; the near-meaning group gathers words for a sitting at the table and for ground grain.
note.cn: 形近组收「粉」这一族词和它的磨坊；近义组收表示围桌用餐的词与表示磨碎谷物的词。

entries.definition: Like meal or covered with meal; also used of dry, pale food.
entries.definitionCN: 像粗粉的、覆着粉的；也形容食物干而发白。

entries.definition: The time when a meal is normally eaten.
entries.definitionCN: 通常吃饭的时间。

entries.definition: Oats ground into meal, or the porridge made from them.
entries.definitionCN: 燕麦磨成的粗粉，或由此煮成的粥。

entries.definition: A building or machine that grinds grain.
entries.definitionCN: 磨谷的厂房或机器；磨坊。

entries.definition: The main meal of the day, usually in the evening.
entries.definitionCN: 一天中的正餐，通常指晚餐。

entries.definition: A meal, especially a formal or leisurely one.
entries.definitionCN: 一餐，尤指正式或从容的一顿。

entries.definition: A small amount of food eaten between meals.
entries.definitionCN: 两餐之间吃的一点食物。

entries.definition: Fine powder made by grinding grain, finer than meal.
entries.definitionCN: 谷物磨成的细粉，比粗粉更细。

normalIntro.en: One spelling now holds two histories: a measured hour and a handful of ground grain.
normalIntro.cn: 同一个拼写如今装着两段历史：量出的时刻与一把磨碎的谷物。

normal.en: Old English mǣl meant an appointed time, so the earliest meal was a moment on the clock rather than a plate of food.
normal.cn: 古英语 mǣl 意为约定的时刻，所以最早的 meal 是钟表上的一个时刻，而不是一盘食物。

normal.en: The flour sense comes from melu, a different Old English word that later merged with mǣl in spelling.
normal.cn: 「粉」的义项来自 melu，一个后来在拼写上并入 mǣl 的另一个古英语词。

normal.en: Mealtime and oatmeal are compounds: one adds time, the other adds the grain that was ground.
normal.cn: mealtime 与 oatmeal 都是复合词：一个加上时间，一个加上被磨碎的谷物。

normal.en: The adjective mealy adds -y to meal, giving the idea of something powdery on the surface.
normal.cn: 形容词 mealy 在 meal 后加 -y，表示表面有粉末状的东西。

normal.en: Cornmeal and oatmeal keep the old powder sense alive in kitchens today.
normal.cn: cornmeal 与 oatmeal 让古老的粉末义项至今仍活在厨房里。

abstract.en: A meal is a clock and a table at once: time measured out, then filled with food.
abstract.cn: 一餐既是钟也是桌：先把时间量出来，再用食物把它填满。

abstract.en: Two words that once meant different things can end up spelled the same, and a dictionary entry quietly holds both.
abstract.cn: 两个原本意思不同的词可能最终拼写相同，而一个词条会安静地把二者都收下。

abstract.en: Grinding turns hard grain into soft powder, which is why the same word can name a dinner and a bag of feed.
abstract.cn: 磨碎把坚硬的谷物变成软粉，所以同一个词既能称一顿饭，也能称一袋饲料。

examples.en: We usually have a quiet meal before the school bus arrives.
examples.cn: 校车到来之前，我们通常安静地吃一顿饭。

examples.en: She cooked a simple meal of rice and vegetables.
examples.cn: 她做了一顿简单的米饭加蔬菜。

examples.en: The old mill still grinds corn into meal.
examples.cn: 那座老磨坊仍把玉米磨成粗粉。

sensesIntro.en: The core is food at a set time; the senses then split between the occasion, the food, the ground grain and industrial powders.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是按时吃的那顿饭；义项由此分成吃饭的场合、食物本身、磨碎的谷物与工业粗粉。

intro.en: The entry is held together by a Germanic time word, a Germanic flour word, and a handful of English compounds and suffixes.
intro.cn: 这个词条由日耳曼语的时间词、日耳曼语的面粉词，以及若干英语复合词与后缀共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Neither Germanic word behind meal has a reliable Latin cognate; Latin molere belongs to the grinding family but is not the source of this word.
latinIntro.cn: meal 背后的两个日耳曼词都没有可靠的拉丁同族词；拉丁语 molere 属「磨」的词族，却不是这个词的来源。

definition_en: to intend or signify something; also the middle value of a set of numbers, or unkind and unwilling to spend
core_image: 一句含混的话被手指向它真正要说的那件事，旁边天平恰好停在正中

senses.title: To have a sense
senses.definition: to have as a meaning, said of a word, sign or gesture
senses.definitionCN: 指词语、符号或手势所具有的意思
senses.example: What does this symbol mean?
senses.exampleCN: 这个符号表示什么？
senses.why: The Old English verb mænan meant 'to intend, signify', and a word's sense is what it intends.
senses.whyCN: 古英语动词 mænan 意为「意图、意指」，而词的意思就是它所意图的东西。

senses.title: To be a sign of
senses.definition: to be a sign or indication of something else
senses.definitionCN: 作为另一件事的迹象或征兆
senses.example: A red sky at night means fair weather tomorrow.
senses.exampleCN: 傍晚的红霞意味着明天天气晴好。
senses.why: A sign points to what it intends, so the verb extends from words to natural signs.
senses.whyCN: 符号指向它所意指之物，于是这个动词从词语扩展到自然征兆。

senses.title: To intend to do
senses.definition: to have something in mind as a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 把某事放在心里作为目的
senses.example: I mean to finish the report tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 我打算今晚把报告写完。
senses.why: Intention is the inward side of meaning: what a person means is what he intends.
senses.whyCN: 意图是「意思」的内面：一个人意指什么，就是他打算什么。

senses.title: The average of a set
senses.definition: the value obtained by adding all the numbers and dividing by how many there are
senses.definitionCN: 把全部数值相加再除以个数所得的值
senses.example: Add the values and divide by five to get the mean.
senses.exampleCN: 把这些值相加再除以五，就得到平均值。
senses.why: This sense comes from a different source: Old French meien 'middle', from Latin medianus, not from the English verb.
senses.whyCN: 这一义出自另一来源：古法语 meien「中间」，上溯拉丁 medianus，与英语动词无关。

senses.title: The middle between extremes
senses.definition: a middle point equally distant from two extremes
senses.definitionCN: 与两个极端等距的中间点
senses.example: The golden mean lies between excess and defect.
senses.exampleCN: 中庸之道位于过度与不足之间。
senses.why: The same 'middle' sense serves ethics as well as arithmetic, naming the point that is neither too much nor too little.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「中间」义既用于算术也用于伦理，指既不过多也不过少的那一点。

senses.title: Unkind in manner
senses.definition: unkind, spiteful or deliberately hurtful
senses.definitionCN: 不友善、带恶意或故意伤人的
senses.example: It was mean of him to laugh at her mistake.
senses.exampleCN: 他嘲笑她的错误，未免刻薄。
senses.why: The adjective comes from a third source, Old English gemæne 'common, shared', whose sense sank from 'common' to 'inferior' and then to 'petty'.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词出自第三个来源，古英语 gemæne「共同的、共享的」，词义从「共同」降到「低劣」，再降到「小气」。

senses.title: Stingy with money
senses.definition: unwilling to spend or share what one has
senses.definitionCN: 不愿花钱或不愿分享所有
senses.example: He is too mean to buy a second chair.
senses.exampleCN: 他太吝啬，连第二把椅子都不肯买。
senses.why: A person who keeps everything for himself is 'common' in the old sense of ordinary and small, and the word settled into stinginess.
senses.whyCN: 把一切都留给自己的人在旧义上显得「普通而小气」，于是这个词固定为吝啬。

senses.title: Remarkable in the phrase 'no mean'
senses.titleCN: 固定说法中意为「不小的」
senses.definition: not small or easy, used in the fixed phrase no mean feat
senses.definitionCN: 不小、不容易，用于固定说法「不小的成就」
senses.example: Finishing the climb in one day was no mean feat.
senses.exampleCN: 一天之内爬完这段路可不是小事。
senses.why: The phrase works by understatement: it denies the small reading of the adjective in order to praise.
senses.whyCN: 这个说法用反语：否定形容词「小」的那一面，从而达到称赞。

intro.en: Mean has three separate sources that happen to share one spelling: the verb 'to intend' from Old English mænan, the noun 'average' from Old French meien and Latin medianus, and the adjective 'petty, stingy' from Old English gemæne 'common'.
intro.cn: mean 有三个恰好同形的来源：表示「意图」的动词出自古英语 mænan；表示「平均值」的名词出自古法语 meien 与拉丁 medianus；表示「小气、刻薄」的形容词出自古英语 gemæne「共同的」。

items.en: Mænan meant 'to intend, signify'. Its deeper Germanic origin is not settled; the usual comparison with German meinen is a family resemblance rather than a proved derivation.
items.cn: mænan 意为「意图、意指」。其更早的日耳曼来源无定论；通常把它与德语 meinen 相比，那只是同族相似，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Gemæne meant 'common, shared'. The sense passed from 'common' to 'ordinary, inferior' and then to 'petty, stingy', a downward slide recorded in Middle English.
items.cn: gemæne 意为「共同的、共享的」。词义从「共同」经「普通、低劣」滑向「小气、吝啬」，这一下移在中古英语中已有记录。

items.en: Meien 'middle' entered English in the fourteenth century as the name of the middle value, and it is the source of the average sense.
items.cn: meien「中间」在十四世纪进入英语，指居中的那个数值，是平均值义的来源。

items.en: Medianus 'of the middle' comes from medius 'middle', the same root that gives median, medium and mediate.
items.cn: medianus「中间的」出自 medius「中间」，同一词根还给出 median、medium、mediate。

items.en: English spelling merged the three histories into one written form, which is why a single entry must keep verb, average and adjective apart.
items.cn: 英语拼写把这三段历史并成一个书写形式，因此同一个词条必须把动词、平均值与形容词分开。

items.en: Exact first citations for each strand are approximate: the verb is Old English, the average noun is fourteenth-century, and the stingy adjective is later Middle English.
items.cn: 三条线索的确切首见书证都只是约数：动词属古英语，平均值名词属十四世纪，吝啬形容词属中古英语后期。

note.en: Group one holds forms and relatives that are easily mistaken for the same word; group two holds words that share one of the three meanings.
note.cn: 第一组是容易被当成同一个词的形式与亲属词；第二组是分别与三种含义之一相近的词。

entries.definition: The third-person singular of the verb, and separately a plural noun meaning 'resources'; it is not the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 动词的第三人称单数，另有一个表示「资源、手段」的复数名词；都不是那个形容词。

entries.definition: The past tense and participle of the verb; the spelling no longer shows the vowel of the base.
entries.definitionCN: 动词的过去式与过去分词；拼写已看不出原形元音。

entries.definition: From the same Latin root as the average sense, but it names the middle item of an ordered set, not the sum divided by the count.
entries.definitionCN: 与平均值义同出拉丁词根，但指按序排列后居中的那一项，而非总和除以个数。

entries.definition: Latin medius as a noun: the middle, or a means between two sides; it has nothing to do with intending.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁 medius 的名词形式：中间，或两端之间的媒介；与「意图」无关。

entries.definition: The everyday word for the sum divided by the count; mean is its technical doublet in statistics.
entries.definitionCN: 日常说法，指总和除以个数；在统计中 mean 是它的技术性同义词。

entries.definition: To be a sign of something, close to the 'be a sign' sense of mean.
entries.definitionCN: 作为某事的符号，接近 mean 的「预示」义。

entries.definition: To have a purpose, the plain equivalent of the 'plan' sense.
entries.definitionCN: 怀有目的，是「打算」义的直白对应词。

entries.definition: Unwilling to spend or share, the direct synonym of the adjective in its money sense.
entries.definitionCN: 不愿花钱或分享，是形容词在钱财义上的直接同义词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定说法与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Three histories share one spelling: intend, middle, and common-turned-petty.
normal.cn: 三段历史共用一种拼写：意图、中间、由「共同」转来的小气。

normal.en: The verb is irregular in sound but regular in pattern: means, meant, meant, meaning.
normal.cn: 动词读音不规则但形式规律：三单、过去式、过去分词、现在分词依次为 means、meant、meant、meaning。

normal.en: Fixed phrases sort the senses: mean to do, mean well, the mean value, no mean feat.
normal.cn: 固定说法把义项分开：打算做、出于好意、平均值、不小的成就。

normal.en: The average sense came through French, so it belongs with median and medium rather than with the verb.
normal.cn: 平均值义经法语而来，因此它与 median、medium 同族，而不属于动词那一支。

normal.en: The unkind sense began as 'common', which then meant 'ordinary' and finally 'petty'.
normal.cn: 刻薄义起于「共同的」，再变成「普通的」，最后成了「小气的」。

abstract.en: Picture a hand pointing at the one thing a vague sentence was trying to say.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手指出一句含混的话真正想说的那件事。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of scales settling exactly level, with equal weights on both sides.
abstract.cn: 想象一架天平恰好停在水平位置，两边重量相等。

abstract.en: Picture a man counting coins twice before he will spend a single one.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人把硬币数了两遍才肯花掉一枚。

examples.en: A green light means that the road is clear.
examples.cn: 绿灯表示道路畅通。

examples.en: The mean of the class scores rose after the extra lesson.
examples.cn: 加课之后，全班成绩的平均值上升了。

examples.en: It was mean of them to leave her out of the invitation.
examples.cn: 他们把她排除在邀请之外，实在刻薄。

dict_mnemonic.text: 动词那一支表示「意图、意指」；平均值那一支来自法语里的「中间」；形容词那一支从「共同的」滑到「普通」，再滑到「小气」。三支同形，要按上下文分开。

root: 三条互不同源的线索合成一个拼写：动词出自古英语 mænan「意图、意指」，更早来源无定论；平均值义出自古法语 meien「中间」，上溯拉丁 medianus、medius；形容词义出自古英语 gemæne「共同的」，词义下滑为「低劣、小气」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses come from three histories: intending and signifying, the middle value, and the small or petty. The entry keeps them apart so that no sentence is read through the wrong history.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项来自三段历史：意图与意指、居中的数值、以及小气刻薄。本词条把它们分开，免得用错历史去读一个句子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand points at what a sentence intends, while a balance beside it rests exactly level.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手指出一句话所意图的东西，旁边的天平恰好水平。

branches.en: SIGNIFY: a word and a red sky both point to what they intend.
branches.cn: 意指：一个词与一片红霞都指向它们所意图的东西。

branches.en: INTEND: purpose is what a person means to do.
branches.cn: 意图：目的就是一个人打算做的事。

branches.en: THE MIDDLE: the average and the golden mean are one position seen numerically and ethically.
branches.cn: 中间：平均值与中庸是同一点在数字与伦理上的两个看法。

branches.en: COMMON TO PETTY: the adjective slid from shared to ordinary to stingy.
branches.cn: 由共同到小气：形容词从「共享」滑到「普通」再到「吝啬」。

branches.en: UNDERSTATEMENT: denying 'small' is a way of saying 'large'.
branches.cn: 反语：否定「小」，正是说「大」。

intro.en: One spelling serves three families, so the affix view must be split: a Germanic verb, a Germanic adjective, and a Latin root for the middle.
intro.cn: 一种拼写服务于三个词族，因此按语素读时必须拆开：一个日耳曼动词、一个日耳曼形容词，以及一个表示「中间」的拉丁词根。

latinIntro.en: The verb family is Germanic, with no Latin kin; the average sense belongs to Latin medius, which also gives median, medium and mediate.
latinIntro.cn: 动词一族属日耳曼语，没有拉丁同族；平均值义属拉丁 medius，同根还给出 median、medium、mediate。

items.example: The Old English verb is the source of the 'signify' senses.
items.exampleCN: 这个古英语动词是「意指」诸义的来源。

items.example: The adjective began as 'shared' and ended as 'stingy'.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词从「共享」开始，最后落到「吝啬」。

items.example: The Latin root supplies the average and middle senses.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁词根提供平均值与中间诸义。
这个派生形容词给出 median。
我指的是第二扇门。

items.structure: mean + -ing (noun suffix, result of an action)
items.exampleCN: 意思很清楚。

items.meaning: in a petty or stingy way
items.example: He spoke meanly of the offer.
items.exampleCN: 他刻薄地评价那个提议。

items.meaning: the quality of being petty or stingy
items.exampleCN: 他们的吝啬让客人吃惊。

definition_zh: 与此同时；在此期间；其间；那段时间
definition_en: during the time between two events, or at the same time as something else is happening
core_image: 两条并排的时间线都在往前走，中间连着一条细线
scene: 客厅里电视还开着，厨房的水壶已经开始响。She kept stirring the soup; meanwhile the guests arrived one by one.
sceneCN: 这里是「与此同时」（第 2 个义项：两件事并行发生）；句意为她一直搅着汤，与此同时客人陆续到了。

collocations.zh: 与此同时，在别处（戏谑转场语）

derivatives.zh: 由 mean（居间的）与 time 复合而成，与 meanwhile 并行使用，义为「其间；同时」
meanwhile 的前半部分，作形容词时义为「中间的；居中的」
meanwhile 的后半部分，作名词时义为「一段时间」

senses.title: During the interval between two events
senses.titleCN: 在此期间；两件事之间的空当
senses.definition: in the period of time between one event and another
senses.definitionCN: 在一件事与另一件事之间的那段时间里
senses.example: The first film ended at nine; meanwhile the second hall was still filling up.
senses.exampleCN: 第一场电影九点散场，在此期间第二个放映厅还在进人。
senses.why: Meanwhile was built from mean, meaning middle or intervening, and while, meaning a stretch of time, so its first job was to name the gap between two moments.
senses.whyCN: meanwhile 由 mean（中间的、居间的）与 while（一段时间）构成，所以它最初的任务就是命名两个时刻之间的空当。

senses.title: At the same time, as a contrast
senses.definition: at the same time as something else, especially when the two developments are being contrasted
senses.definitionCN: 与另一件事同时发生，尤用于对比两种变化
senses.example: Prices kept rising; meanwhile wages stayed flat.
senses.exampleCN: 物价持续上涨，与此同时工资原地不动。
senses.why: Because the gap between two events is also a span shared by them, the word came to mark two lines of action running side by side.
senses.whyCN: 既然两件事之间的空当也是二者共有的时段，这个词就转而标记两条并排推进的行动线。

senses.title: The time between two events as a noun
senses.definition: the period of time between two events, used with the as a noun
senses.definitionCN: 两件事之间的那段时间，加 the 作名词使用
senses.example: In the meanwhile, the children played in the yard.
senses.exampleCN: 在这段时间里，孩子们在院子里玩。
senses.why: English often turns an adverb of time into a noun by adding the, and the meanwhile names the stretch itself rather than the relation between events.
senses.whyCN: 英语常用加 the 的办法把时间副词变成名词，the meanwhile 指的就是那段时间本身，而不是事件之间的关系。

intro.en: Meanwhile is a compound of two older words: mean in its middle sense and while in its time sense.
intro.cn: meanwhile 是两个更古老的词复合而成：取「中间」义的 mean 与取「时间」义的 while。

items.en: Latin medianus meant middle or central, and it reached English through French as the adjective mean.
items.cn: 拉丁语 medianus 意为中间的、中央的，经法语进入英语，成为形容词 mean。

items.en: Old French meien kept the middle sense and supplied the form that English shortened to mean.
items.cn: 古法语 meien 保留了「中间」的意思，提供了英语缩略为 mean 的词形。

items.en: Old English hwīl meant a period of time, and it is the word behind while.
items.cn: 古英语 hwīl 意为一段时间，是 while 的来源。

items.en: Middle English used the phrase in the mean while, literally in the intervening time.
items.cn: 中古英语使用 in the mean while 这一短语，字面意思是「在居间的那段时间里」。

items.en: The phrase was compressed into the single adverb meanwhile, and a noun use with the followed.
items.cn: 这个短语被压缩成单个副词 meanwhile，随后又出现了加 the 的名词用法。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the compound's two halves and its twin; the near-meaning group collects adverbs of simultaneous timing.
note.cn: 形近组收这个复合词的两半和它的孪生词；近义组收表示同时发生的副词。

entries.definition: A parallel compound meaning the intervening time.
entries.definitionCN: 并行的复合词，意为其间的那段时间。

entries.definition: As an adjective, middle or average.
entries.definitionCN: 作形容词时意为中间的、平均的。

entries.definition: A period of time, or during the time that.
entries.definitionCN: 一段时间，或「在……期间」。

entries.definition: A chiefly British variant of while.
entries.definitionCN: while 的英式变体。

entries.definition: At exactly the same time.
entries.definitionCN: 在同一时刻。

entries.definition: At the same time, often of events running in parallel.
entries.definitionCN: 同时发生，常指并行的事件。

entries.definition: Both at the same time, in one phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，表示同时。

normalIntro.en: The word is a phrase welded into one adverb, built from a middle word and a time word.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个被焊成副词短语的组合，由「中间」的词与「时间」的词搭成。

normal.en: Mean here is not the verb meaning intend; it is the old adjective for middle.
normal.cn: 这里的 mean 不是表示「打算」的动词，而是古老的形容词「中间的」。

normal.en: While is the time word, so meanwhile literally means in the middle of the time.
normal.cn: while 是时间词，所以 meanwhile 字面上就是「在时间中间」。

normal.en: Meantime is built on time instead of while, which is why the two words are so close in meaning.
normal.cn: meantime 用 time 而不是 while 来构成，所以两个词的意思非常接近。

normal.en: The phrase in the meanwhile shows the noun use, with the standing before the compound.
normal.cn: in the meanwhile 展示了名词用法，the 就放在这个复合词前面。

normal.en: The two halves still live separately: mean as middle and while as a stretch of time.
normal.cn: 两半仍然各自独立：mean 表示中间，while 表示一段时间。

abstract.en: Two clocks side by side keep their own pace, and the space between them is the meanwhile.
abstract.cn: 两只并排的钟各走各的，二者之间的空隙就是 meanwhile。

abstract.en: Think of a film cutting between two rooms, the camera saying meanwhile without a word.
abstract.cn: 想一部电影在两个房间之间切换，镜头不说话就完成了「与此同时」。

abstract.en: English often welds a phrase into one word, and meanwhile is a whole clause shrunk to a signal.
abstract.cn: 英语常把短语焊成一个词，meanwhile 就是一整句关系被压缩成一个信号。

examples.en: She kept stirring the soup; meanwhile the guests arrived one by one.
examples.cn: 她一直搅着汤，与此同时客人陆续到了。

examples.en: Prices kept rising; meanwhile wages stayed flat.
examples.cn: 物价持续上涨，与此同时工资原地不动。

examples.en: In the meanwhile, the children played in the yard.
examples.cn: 在这段时间里，孩子们在院子里玩。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「民外」——屋里忙着，民外也在忙；记住 meanwhile 是与此同时。

root: 由 mean（中间的，源自拉丁语 medianus，经古法语 meien 入英语）与 while（一段时间，古英语 hwīl）复合，字面义为「在居间的那段时间里」。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the span shared by two happenings; the senses divide into the interval, the parallel contrast, and the interval treated as a noun.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是两件事共有的那段时间；义项分成居间的空当、并行的对比，以及被当作名词的那段时间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two time lines running forward side by side, joined by a thin line between them.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条并排向前的时间线，中间连着一条细线。

branches.en: two events with a gap between them
branches.cn: 两件事之间留出一段空当

branches.en: two lines of action running at once
branches.cn: 两条行动线同时推进

branches.en: a noun phrase with the in front
branches.cn: 前面加 the 的名词短语

branches.en: a film cutting from one room to another
branches.cn: 电影从一个房间切到另一个房间

branches.en: two graphs rising in opposite directions
branches.cn: 两条曲线朝相反方向走

intro.en: The word is supported by a Latin-derived middle adjective, an Old English time noun, and the twin compound built on time.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁来源的「中间」形容词、古英语的时间名词，以及以 time 构成的孪生复合词共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: The first half of the compound goes back to Latin medianus, so the word carries one genuine Latin cognate inside it.
latinIntro.cn: 这个复合词的前半部分可追溯到拉丁语 medianus，因此词内确实含有一个拉丁同源成分。
